articles.headline: Actor Yash advises fans to watch Ramayana with an open mind
articles.summary: Kannada actor Yash, discussing the upcoming cinematic adaptation of the Ramayana, urged audiences to refrain from finding faults and instead watch the film with an open mind. He highlighted the significant use of VFX in the production to bring the legendary epic to life, describing it as the rise of a legend and a milestone for Indian cinema.

articles.headline: Dia Mirza Rekhi marks 25 years in the Indian film industry
articles.summary: Actor Dia Mirza Rekhi looks back on her 25-year career since winning the Miss Asia Pacific International crown in 2000. Despite an initial struggle at the box office with her debut Rehnaa Hai Terre Dil Mein, the film gained cult status. She discussed evolving from stardom to producing content she believes in, such as Love Breakups Zindagi and the web series Kaafir.

articles.headline: Health advice and precautions for residents as Delhi AQI levels worsen
articles.summary: As Delhi's Air Quality Index (AQI) worsened to 187 on Monday, health experts have issued advisories to protect vulnerable groups. Recommendations include wearing N95 masks outdoors, using HEPA air purifiers, and avoiding strenuous outdoor activities during peak pollution hours. A diet rich in antioxidants, including citrus fruits and ginger, is also suggested to combat the effects.

articles.headline: Insensitive memes about Tiger Shroff firing incident face online criticism
articles.summary: Social media users and celebrities have criticized the circulation of insensitive memes following the firing incident involving Tiger Shroff's vehicle. YouTuber Ashish Chanchlani and journalist Rajdeep Sardesai pointed out that joking about potentially fatal attacks is inappropriate. The backlash highlights concerns over the growing trend of turning serious news into content for likes.

articles.headline: Sanjana Sanghi shares childhood memories of celebrating Diwali in Delhi
articles.summary: Actor Sanjana Sanghi reflected on her childhood memories of Diwali in Delhi, highlighting the multicultural traditions of her Punjabi, Marwari, and Gujarati family. She spoke about the annual tradition of 'Diwali ki safai' and festive card games. Sanghi expressed that returning home for the festival allows her to relive these cherished moments through traditional food and decorations.

articles.headline: Tamil actor Karthik Sabesh passes away at 37 in Chennai
articles.summary: Tamil film actor Karthik Sabesh, known for roles in films like Vallavan and Udhayan, passed away in Chennai at the age of 37. His death comes just days after the passing of his uncle, music composer Deva. Karthik belonged to a prominent musical family; his father is the late music composer Sabesh. Final rites were performed at the Valasaravakkam burial ground.

articles.headline: Nepal bans screening of Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan film
articles.summary: The Ministry of Communication and Information Technology in Nepal has denied permission for the public screening of Udta Teer, starring Ayushmann Khurrana and Sara Ali Khan. The decision followed a review by the Central Film Censor Board, which classified the film under a category restricted by law. The spy-comedy was originally slated for an international release on October 23.

articles.headline: Deepthi Jeevanji discusses how sports success earned her family respect
articles.summary: Para-athlete Deepthi Jeevanji shared her personal journey, noting that her international sporting success has changed how her community treats her family. Previously facing negativity due to her intellectual impairment, she now receives respect from villagers. Deepthi, whose parents worked as daily-wage labourers, aims to coach young girls to pursue their dreams in athletics.

articles.headline: Ferris wheels and carnival stalls draw crowds during festive season
articles.summary: Giant Ferris wheels and traditional rides have become a major attraction at the Red Fort grounds during the Ramlila and Dussehra festivities. The carnival stalls, which offer various games and food, continue to draw large crowds of visitors. These traditional fairs remain a highlight of the festive season in Delhi, with celebrations expected to continue until late October.

articles.headline: Bollywood celebrities attend various Durga Puja pandals in Mumbai
articles.summary: Top Bollywood actors and filmmakers, including Vicky Kaushal, Alia Bhatt, and Imtiaz Ali, were spotted at various Durga Puja pandals across Mumbai. The celebrities were seen in traditional attire, participating in rituals and soaking in the festive spirit. Other attendees included Ektaa R Kapoor, Shreya Ghoshal, and Sumona Chakravarti, adding glamour to the religious celebrations.

articles.headline: Cricketer Suryakumar Yadav makes ramp debut at Lakmé Fashion Week
articles.summary: Indian cricketer Suryakumar Yadav walked the ramp as the showstopper for the brand Ethnix by Raymond at Lakmé Fashion Week in Mumbai. He wore a tailored long jacket featuring intricate Greshm embroidery paired with relaxed-fit trousers. The collection aimed to showcase a contemporary version of the modern Indian man through traditional yet stylish fashion.

articles.headline: Exhibition in Delhi showcases artistic evolution of V Ramesh
articles.summary: A new exhibition titled 'Sacred Spaces' at Bikaner House, Delhi, features the early figurative and devotional works of contemporary artist V Ramesh. The preview event included a performance by dancer Navtej Johar, which complemented the allegorical imagery of Ramesh's art. The collection traces his career from the 1980s to the present, focusing on themes like the life of fisherfolk.

articles.headline: Student protesters force closure of Louvre Museum in Paris
articles.summary: The Louvre Museum in Paris was forced to close to visitors after students and protesters blocked its entrances. The demonstration is part of a wave of unrest across France, where clashes with police have led to more than 2,400 arrests since mid-October. Protesters are demanding better school funding and an end to what they describe as police repression during nationwide strikes.

articles.headline: Artha Bharat Relocates Two Funds to Abu Dhabi Over Tax Uncertainty
articles.summary: Artha Bharat Investment Managers IFSC is shifting $112 million from GIFT City to Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) citing tax uncertainty and compliance burdens. The firm is pursuing a matter regarding disallowed tax deductions under Section 80LA. The move allows for smaller ticket sizes ($55,000 in ADGM vs $150,000 in GIFT City) to widen its investor base.

articles.headline: HDFC Bank Plans Overseas Branch Expansion Under New Leadership
articles.summary: HDFC Bank, India’s largest private lender, plans to expand its international branch network as incoming CEO Anup Bagchi takes charge. Outgoing CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan noted that limited global presence previously constrained the bank's ability to mobilize foreign currency deposits. The bank currently operates branches in Bahrain, Singapore, Hong Kong, and Dubai.

articles.headline: Retail Auto Sales Rise 2% During Navratri Despite Car Sales Slump
articles.summary: Automobile retail sales during Navratri grew 2% year-on-year to 1.03 million units, though passenger vehicle sales dropped 14% to 172,087 units. Two-wheeler sales rose 6% while commercial vehicles increased 14%. Fada data suggests the drop in car sales is due to an exceptionally high base set in 2025 following previous GST cuts and significant pent-up demand.

articles.headline: Sivakasi Eyes Global Fireworks Markets as Export Demand Rises
articles.summary: The Indian fireworks hub of Sivakasi is targeting international markets as European and US customers seek alternatives to Chinese supplies. The Tamil Nadu government plans a policy to align production with global standards. Following a Supreme Court order allowing green crackers, the town accounts for 85% of India's organized fireworks trade worth nearly ₹6,000 crore.

articles.headline: Rising Overnight Rates Indicate Surge in India Liquidity Demand
articles.summary: The RBI’s overnight variable rate repo auction is expected to see strong demand as declining surplus liquidity pushes up rates. The weighted average call rate rose to 5.66% on Monday, nearing the marginal standing facility rate. Factors including festival-related currency leakage and cash reserve ratio restrictions have contributed to the tightening liquidity conditions.

articles.headline: Generic Brands Capture 74% Volume Share in India Semaglutide Market
articles.summary: Six months after patent expiry, generic versions of the weight-loss drug semaglutide account for 74% of monthly volumes in India. Total volumes rose 281% from February to 434,000 units in September. While sales value grew 135% to ₹113 crore, the market is shifting from initial hype to stable, doctor-driven prescriptions for metabolic diseases.

articles.headline: BVG India Shifts Focus to High Margin Long-Term Contracts
articles.summary: Integrated services provider BVG India is prioritizing long-term, high-margin contracts for facilities management and ambulance services. The company reported FY26 revenue of ₹4,128 crore, up 25% year-on-year. Profit after tax rose 28% to ₹284 crore. The firm recently received Sebi approval for an IPO which includes a fresh issue of ₹300 crore and an offer for sale.

articles.headline: India Targets Leadership in 6G Technology Through Satellite Integration
articles.summary: GSMA APAC head Julian Gorman states that satellite technology will complement mobile networks to bridge connectivity gaps as India advances toward 6G. India is emerging as a global model for next-generation telecom, with data consumption expected to rise to 75GB per month by 2030. Regulation and spectrum agreements at WRC-27 will be key for mass adoption.

articles.headline: Prestige Estates to Launch 40,000 Crore Worth of Homes in H2
articles.summary: Realty firm Prestige Estates Projects Ltd plans to launch residential properties worth ₹40,000 crore in the second half of the 2026-27 fiscal year. This represents a 2.5 times increase from the first half, as the company looks to capitalize on festival demand across 23.14 million square feet of planned development.

articles.headline: Tinder and Hinge Introduce Biometric Verification and India Safety Features
articles.summary: Match Group has launched India-specific safety measures for Tinder and Hinge, including screenshot blocking and mandatory video selfie verification. The company invests $125 million annually in safety. New features aim to combat romance scams and AI-generated fake profiles while catering to GenZ preferences for social, low-pressure dating experiences.

articles.headline: CXMT Swings to Profit as Global Memory Chip Prices Surge
articles.summary: Chinese chipmaker CXMT reported a preliminary nine-month profit of up to 132.5 billion yuan, reversing a net loss from the previous year. Revenue is expected to reach 270 billion yuan as global demand for memory components drives prices higher. This follows a broader boom in the memory-chip sector fueled by AI and consumer technology needs.

articles.headline: Visa and Billing Firms Pilot AI-Powered Automated Invoice Payments
articles.summary: Visa is partnering with BILL Holdings and Billtrust to pilot AI agents that initiate and complete business invoice payments without human authentication. The solution targets tedious manual review processes for recurring and predictable business expenses, allowing AI to manage the end-to-end payment cycle.

articles.headline: Microsoft Executive Warns Enterprises to Restrict AI Agent Access
articles.summary: Microsoft VP Mike Yeh warned that companies deploying AI agents must grant 'least amount of privilege' to prevent overreach into sensitive data. Speaking on the 2026 Digital Defense Report, Yeh noted that while AI compresses attack cycles, enterprises must patch old vulnerabilities first. Microsoft also announced new sovereign cloud control options for Azure users.

articles.headline: YatriKart and MMG Group to Open 1,000 Quick-Stop Stores
articles.summary: Transit retail chain YatriKart partnered with MMG Group in a ₹120 crore deal to launch 1,000 convenience stores across India over five years. MMG Group, a major Coca-Cola and McDonald’s partner, will fund infrastructure while YatriKart manages operations. The stores will target high-footfall locations like petrol pumps, highways, and transit hubs.

articles.headline: Nirmala Sitharaman Proposes Global Framework to Address Economic Sanction Fallout
articles.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman called for a multilateral convention on economic sanctions to protect countries beyond those directly targeted. Speaking at IMF-World Bank meetings, she highlighted macrocritical implications of primary and secondary sanctions on energy and trade. She noted India's growth remains strong at 7% despite global financial volatility.

articles.headline: India Goods Producers Regain Pricing Power with 10% Price Hike
articles.summary: Indian goods producers saw a nearly 10% year-on-year increase in prices during H1FY27, ending three years of market apathy. Mining products and manufacturing led the surge, with output prices consistently higher than input costs. This shift indicates that manufacturers have successfully passed on costs to consumers for the first time since 2023.

articles.headline: Finance Ministry Gives In-Principle Nod to Polysilicon Support Scheme
articles.summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy received initial approval for a scheme to support domestic polysilicon manufacturing. Polysilicon is a critical raw material for solar panels. India aims for 30GW of domestic capacity by 2030, requiring ₹25,000 crore in investment. The scheme aims to plug the last missing link in India's solar manufacturing chain.

articles.headline: Yes Bank Decides Against Immediate Capital Raise Despite Buffer Concerns
articles.summary: Yes Bank CFO Niranjan Banodkar stated the bank has no immediate plans to raise capital, despite a potential drop in its CET1 ratio to 11.4% following bond reinstatements. The bank intends to use existing buffers and deferred tax assets. Banodkar emphasized that while current levels are not ideal, the decision to raise funds remains a commercial evaluation.

articles.headline: IndusInd General Insurance Names Sharad Mathur as New MD and CEO
articles.summary: Sharad Mathur has been appointed as the Managing Director and CEO of IndusInd General Insurance Company Ltd. Mathur previously led Universal Sompo General Insurance for six years. The appointment follows statutory approvals and comes as the company focuses on digital transformation and strengthening its distribution and risk management capabilities.

articles.headline: Oxfam Report Links Rising Rural Women's Labor Participation to Distress
articles.summary: A study by Oxfam suggests the rise in rural Indian women's labor participation—nearly doubling to 47.6% since 2017-18—is driven by economic distress rather than growth. Most are working as unpaid helpers in family enterprises or in agriculture. Regular salaried jobs for women dropped to 8%, indicating a shift toward precarious and unpaid roles instead of secure incomes.

articles.headline: Piramal Finance Open to Acquisitions While Expanding Urban Lending
articles.summary: Piramal Finance MD Jairam Sridharan expects a measured second half of FY27, focusing on urban and semi-urban markets. The company is evaluating inorganic growth opportunities to build capabilities in education and tractor finance. Sridharan noted that while the festival season may be muted, the company benefits from a credit rating upgrade and lower borrowing costs.

articles.headline: PM Modi Calls for National Unity Against Enemies During Dussehra
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged political parties and institutions to stand together for national interest during Dussehra celebrations in New Delhi. He emphasized the goal of a self-reliant India and stated that the spirit of 'Ram Rajya' involves zero discrimination. Modi remarked that victory ultimately belongs to those standing with truth and humanity.

articles.headline: GIFT City AIFs Receive Tax Notices Over Dividend Surcharge Disputes
articles.summary: Category III Alternative Investment Funds in GIFT City have reportedly received tax notices for surcharges on dividends and interest, despite existing exemptions. Tax experts believe the notices may stem from system errors or misinterpretations of the Finance Act 2023. These funds are generally liable for a flat 10% tax without the additional surcharges applicable to domestic funds.

articles.headline: PSBs Outperform Private Sector Lenders in Recent Market Returns
articles.summary: State-owned banks have seen a 5.5% index rise over the past year, while the Nifty Private Bank index fell 4.36%. Analysts attribute the shift to strong Q2 results and higher return on equity for PSBs. However, private banks maintain a valuation edge, trading at nearly 2x price-to-book compared to 1.15x for PSBs, as investors weigh the sustainability of public sector gains.

articles.headline: Direct Mutual Fund Plans Gain Traction in Long-Term SIP Assets
articles.summary: The share of direct mutual fund SIP assets held for over five years more than doubled to 16.6% in September 2026. While regular plans still dominate with ₹4.77 trillion in assets, direct plans are growing due to lower expense ratios and digital platform adoption. Among SIPs less than a year old, direct plans now account for 32.3% of the total share.

articles.headline: Global Stocks Fall as AI Investment Concerns Spark Market Dip
articles.summary: Global markets declined after a South Korean AI data center firm's poor stock debut reignited worries about the sustainability of tech spending. S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures fell as investors became more selective about AI stories. Concurrently, Brent crude prices reached a five-month high of $111 per barrel due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia and the Gulf.

articles.headline: UltraTech Cement Maintains Market Lead Despite Persistent Cost Pressures
articles.summary: UltraTech Cement reported a 19% revenue rise in Q2FY27 with volumes growing 13%, but Ebitda per tonne fell slightly due to high fuel and freight costs. The company is scaling its new cables and wires business, UltraVolt, and remains on track to reach 240 mtpa capacity by FY28. Analysts project margin recovery as demand picks up post-monsoon.

articles.headline: Crompton Greaves Reports 18% Sales Growth Aided by Energy Efficient Fans
articles.summary: Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals saw double-digit growth in Q2, led by a 40% surge in BLDC energy-efficient fans. Exports hit a quarterly high, rising 70%. While input cost inflation weighed on gross margins, cost efficiencies helped operating margins improve. The firm aims for an Ebitda margin of 11-12% by FY29 through brand refreshing and portfolio expansion.

articles.headline: PFRDA Launches NPS Central Platform for Unified Pension Account Management
articles.summary: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority launched NPS Central, a digital hub allowing subscribers to manage accounts across multiple recordkeeping agencies. Features include AI-assisted onboarding, paperless KYC, and consolidated dashboards. The platform also offers NPS Swasthya, which integrates an investment corpus with super top-up health insurance.

articles.headline: Centrist Politics Crumble in Europe Amid Economic Stagnation and Riots
articles.summary: Europe's centrist parties are losing ground to far-right and far-left populists as citizens express dissatisfaction with low growth and high inflation. In France, 69% of the population is dissatisfied with democracy following widespread riots over living costs. Similar trends are visible in Germany, Italy, and Poland, where traditional parties are losing their working-class base.

articles.headline: India Power Sector Under-Investment Threatens to Undermine Renewable Gains
articles.summary: A structural gap in India's old power sector—comprising coal, hydro, and distribution grids—is creating evening shortages despite solar growth. Capacity for non-intermittent power has fallen by 25% relative to peak demand since 2016. Experts warn that debt-strapped distribution companies must invest in network upgrades to handle increasing renewable integration and AI-driven demand.

articles.headline: Civil Aviation Ministry Scrutinizes Airport Baggage Weighing Discrepancies
articles.summary: The Ministry of Civil Aviation is investigating complaints that airport baggage scales weigh heavier than home scales, leading to disputed excess charges. MP Ajeet Madhavrao Gopchade sought a nationwide audit and mandatory scientific calibration of weighing machines. A previous survey suggested 60% of flyers experienced higher baggage weights at airport check-in.

articles.headline: Trump Administration Announces 8 Billion Aid for Farmers to Offset Diesel
articles.summary: The US government will provide $8 billion in one-time payments to farmers to help cover rising fuel costs ahead of midterm elections. Diesel prices reached $6.50 a gallon in September following global supply disruptions. The aid program targets Model 2026 crop losses, aiming to ease financial burdens on a key voting base struggling with massive inventories and limited demand.

articles.headline: Delhi Airport Passenger Traffic Rises 5% to 38.5 Million in H1
articles.summary: Indira Gandhi International Airport reported a 5% increase in total passenger traffic for the first half of FY27, reaching 38.5 million travelers. Domestic traffic rose to 28.1 million while international traffic reached 10.4 million. Air Traffic Movements also jumped 6.9%. Operated by DIAL, the airport recorded its highest-ever half-yearly traffic volume during this period.

articles.headline: Manipur CM Meets Opposition as Protests Erupt Over Civilian Killings
articles.summary: Manipur CM N. Biren Singh met INDIA bloc leaders to discuss the law and order crisis following the killing of three Meitei firewood collectors by suspected militants. A 48-hour strike paralyzed the valley districts, with protesters blocking roads in Imphal. The opposition claimed the state government has completely failed to curb the ongoing ethnic conflict that began in 2023.

articles.headline: Silent shareholders hold the key to Tata Motors’ Iveco deal
articles.summary: Tata Motors requires support from 80% of Iveco's shareholders to complete its €3.9 billion acquisition and delist the Italian truck maker. Current data shows that roughly three in four investors who missed recent meetings must be won over. If acceptance falls between 66.67% and 80%, Tata can proceed with the purchase but cannot delist or restructure the company.

articles.headline: India Inc prepares for muted salary hikes in 2027
articles.summary: Rising costs, geopolitical uncertainty, and a sluggish job market are expected to keep compensation budgets tight for Indian companies in 2027. Experts project nominal salary hikes of 9.1%, similar to 2026. Firms are likely to exercise greater discipline, reserving bigger rewards for top performers as consumer demand remains under pressure.

articles.headline: Government to overhaul tax refund schemes for Indian exporters
articles.summary: The government has set up two panels to review the RoDTEP and RoSCTL schemes, which refund domestic taxes to exporters. The move aims to make payouts more targeted as global uncertainties weigh on shipments. The proposed changes follow recommendations for better fund utilization and could be discussed during upcoming Union budget deliberations.

articles.headline: New clean fuel norms to impact Indian car buyers
articles.summary: The government will implement CAFE-III and BS VII norms over the next three years to promote cleaner fuels. This will push carmakers to expand lineups of EVs, hybrids, and CNG vehicles. While the transition will help Indian vehicles meet global standards, it is expected to increase car prices due to investments in advanced engines and emission control technology.

articles.headline: South Korean tech stocks slide on AI investment jitters
articles.summary: Shares of South Korean tech giants fell as investors grew impatient for evidence of AI success. Elice Group crashed 30% on its debut, while SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics dropped 4.9% and 3.2% respectively. Analysts are closely watching upcoming AI firm results to determine if the global industry can meet its performance promises.

articles.headline: Indians show high trust in healthcare despite cost concerns
articles.summary: A survey by Ipsos reveals that 68% of Indians trust their healthcare system and quality of treatment, ranking ahead of Australia and South Korea. However, the cost of accessing treatment remains the top concern for 42% of respondents, followed by low standards of cleanliness (28%) and poor safety (25%).

articles.headline: Global economic shifts and AI adoption impact India growth
articles.summary: Global growth remains concentrated, with China, India, and the US contributing nearly 60% of expansion in 2026. While India maintains a robust growth trajectory, it lags in AI model development despite high adoption potential. Experts suggest India must strengthen its national balance sheet and improve its net international investment position to remain resilient.

articles.headline: Indians pay high grey market premiums for iPhone Duo
articles.summary: Extreme scarcity of Apple’s iPhone Duo in India has led buyers to pay premiums of up to ₹50,000 in the grey market. With only 6,000 units expected in the first week, the ₹2,99,900 device is seeing high demand from social-status seekers. Authorized retailers report receiving only a fraction of requested stock due to supply rationing.

articles.headline: US Secretary Rubio signals near completion of India trade deal
articles.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated in Mumbai that India and the US are very close to finalizing a trade agreement. Rubio described India as a key strategic partner and an important commercial business ally. Bilateral trade reached $140.76 billion in FY26, with India maintaining a trade surplus of $33.9 billion.

articles.headline: Health ministry declares new pharmacist service rules invalid
articles.summary: A row has erupted as the Union health ministry declared the Pharmacy Council of India's (PCI) new recruitment and promotion regulations for government pharmacists invalid. The ministry claims the rules were issued without central approval. The PCI maintains it acted within statutory powers to reform the profession and address long-standing pay scale issues.

articles.headline: Fortum cancels sale of Glida EV charging network
articles.summary: Finnish utility Fortum Oyj has scrapped plans to sell its Glida EV charging network in India to JBM Group promoters. Fortum will now continue to operate the brand, which has 961 charging points, independently. The decision comes as India's electric vehicle adoption rises, with EV sales crossing 10% in the January-October 2026 period.

articles.headline: Auto part makers form global tie-ups for advanced tech
articles.summary: Indian firms Sona Comstar, Gabriel India, and Varroc Engineering are partnering with global companies to gain a technological edge. The collaborations focus on powertrains, ADAS, automotive electronics, and EV batteries. The strategy aims to help Indian suppliers move up the value chain as global carmakers increase investments in the Indian market.

articles.headline: Investors seek new defensive sectors as IT and FMCG stall
articles.summary: Traditional defensive sectors like IT and FMCG are losing favor as they face slowing growth and rising competition. The Nifty IT index has remained flat over three years, while FMCG fell 16%. Investors are now looking for stability in healthcare, utilities, and financials, as well as income-generating assets like REITs and InvITs.

articles.headline: Gene-edited crops designed to alert farmers of stress
articles.summary: Startups like InnerPlant and Insignum AgTech are using gene editing to program plants to emit signals, such as an invisible glow or purple leaves, when under attack by pests or disease. Backed by companies like John Deere, the technology aims to help farmers take targeted action and reduce the overall use of chemical pesticides and herbicides.

articles.headline: India merchandise exports to UK rise 8% in two months
articles.summary: India's merchandise exports to the UK rose to $2.43 billion in August and September, the first two months after the India-UK free trade agreement took effect. Imports from Britain fell 16.8% to $1.36 billion in the same period. Total exports for April-September 2026 reached $7.32 billion, a 7.22% increase year-on-year.

articles.headline: New urban policy mandates access-controlled bypasses for cities
articles.summary: The road transport ministry has finalized a policy to develop ring roads and bypasses as fully access-controlled corridors. The aim is to prevent urban congestion and maintain highway speeds of 100-120 kmph. These projects will feature closed tolling, where motorists pay based on distance travelled, to curb local unregulated development.

articles.headline: Brics grouping seeks alternative payment systems to US dollar
articles.summary: South Africa's High Commissioner Anil Sooklal stated that Brics is focused on trading in local currencies and developing alternative payment platforms to reduce dependence on the US dollar. He emphasized that the push reflects unease among emerging economies regarding US sanctions and financial dominance, rather than a plan for a common Brics currency.

articles.headline: India expresses concern over UN liquidity and unpaid dues
articles.summary: India has voiced concern over the challenging liquidity situation of the United Nations. During a UN General Assembly meeting, Indian counsellor Surendra Adhana highlighted the unacceptably high levels of unpaid assessments owed by the United States. India urged member states to fulfill their financial obligations to ensure the organization's smooth functioning.

articles.headline: RBI tightens scrutiny of large overseas investments by domestic firms
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India is reportedly increasing oversight of large outbound capital flows to contain pressure on the rupee. Banks have been asked to provide details on overseas direct investments exceeding $1 billion. The move comes as the central bank seeks to manage capital outflows amid currency volatility and global economic shifts.

articles.headline: Global sugar market deficit expected to reach 6.28 million tonnes
articles.summary: Green Pool Commodities has raised its estimate for the global sugar market supply deficit to 6.28 million tonnes. The revision is blamed on poor production in major regions including Brazil, India, and the EU. The struggle to cope with the impacts of the El Niño weather anomaly is a significant factor in the tightening global agriculture supply.

articles.headline: India online retail market to cross $90 billion in 2026
articles.summary: Redseer Strategy Consultants reports that India’s online retail market is projected to grow 22-24% in 2026, reaching over $90 billion. This expansion is driven by everyday consumption categories like grocery rather than traditional segments like mobile phones. The growth represents the fastest expansion in five years for the sector.

articles.headline: Nscale and Anthropic in talks for $45 billion AI deal
articles.summary: AI cloud firm Nscale is negotiating a deal to sell computing power to Anthropic, which could be worth approximately $45 billion. The agreement involves infrastructure at Nscale’s Monarch data centre in West Virginia. This follows Nscale's planned initial public offering and highlights the massive scale of investment in AI computing infrastructure.

articles.headline: Meta oversight board finds recurring failures in election moderation
articles.summary: Meta's oversight board reported recurrent enforcement failures in content moderation during elections in the US and Brazil. The board expressed concerns that social media failures could swing electoral results. It highlighted the need for more robust moderation as platforms remain a go-to source for electoral information globally.

articles.headline: Stock trading app Sahi seeks $50 million in funding
articles.summary: Sahi, a trading app founded by former Swiggy CTO Dale Vaz, is in talks to raise $40-50 million at a valuation of up to $500 million. The startup positions itself as a discount broker with AI-powered analytical tools. Sahi aims to compete with established brokers by offering free in-house charting and an AI assistant named Kyro.

articles.headline: Women-led stories gain significant traction in India's OTT boom
articles.summary: Data from Ormax shows that female-led web series in India generate 47% higher peak buzz than male-led shows, despite making up only 22% of content. Series like Mrs. Deshpande and Dabba Cartel are resonating with audiences by exploring themes of identity and social norms. Scarcity of such content is proving to be a cultural advantage.

articles.headline: HDFC Bank core operating profit rises 12.6% in Q2
articles.summary: HDFC Bank reported a 4.7% rise in net profit to ₹19,510 crore for the September quarter. While net interest margins fell to 3.16%, the bank saw strong loan growth in high-yielding retail and business banking segments. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA shrinking to 1.11%, supported by lower slippages during the quarter.

articles.headline: DLF reports surge in Q2 pre-sales led by luxury launches
articles.summary: Real estate major DLF saw pre-sales bookings zoom to ₹3,800 crore in the September quarter, up from ₹657 crore in Q1. The growth was driven by luxury projects like The Dahlias and The Aureva in Gurugram. The company maintains a focus on high margins and cash flow as it prepares for further luxury launches in the National Capital Region.

articles.headline: Canara Bank MD flags bond yield risks for MTM provisions
articles.summary: Canara Bank MD Brajesh Kumar Singh noted that rising government bond yields pose a potential mark-to-market provisioning risk. However, the bank expects strong festive demand for housing and vehicle loans to sustain credit growth. Net profit for the September quarter rose 8.4% to ₹5,175 crore, while net interest income grew 20.39%.

articles.headline: IBC being used by small vendors as recovery tool
articles.summary: Recent insolvency proceedings against Polycab India highlight how operational creditors are using the IBC to exert pressure on large firms, even when debt amounts are relatively small. Experts note that for listed firms, NCLT admission can trigger regulatory disclosures and hurt investor confidence. Courts have cautioned against using IBC as a mere debt-recovery tool.

articles.headline: Qualcomm to cut global workforce in performance-focused layoffs
articles.summary: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon announced global job cuts following annual employee reviews to build a stronger performance culture. The company, which has 52,000 employees, has been impacted by a slump in consumer electronics sales. Qualcomm aims to shift focus toward non-handset businesses like AI data-centres and automotive chips by 2027.

articles.headline: The LaLiT Suri Hospitality Group to invest ₹600 crore
articles.summary: The LaLiT Suri Hospitality Group plans to add 1,000 rooms over five years through an investment of ₹600 crore. Half of the new rooms will be in owned properties in cities like Ahmedabad and Chitrakoot, while the rest will be through management contracts. The group is targeting 20 management contracts to capitalize on domestic travel demand.

articles.headline: Lenders and brokers push for retail participation in Jio IPO
articles.summary: Financial institutions are offering margin funding covering up to 90% of application value to draw retail investors into Jio Platforms' ₹30,213-crore IPO. The push comes amid negative market sentiment. Reliance Industries reportedly released employee salaries 15 days early to encourage participation in the offer, which includes a ₹10,500 crore retail portion.

articles.headline: Match Group eyes India growth despite online fraud concerns
articles.summary: Match Group is doubling down on India for Tinder and Hinge, citing low adoption rates compared to the US. Despite growth optimism, the company is facing scrutiny over dating-app scams. New safety features like screenshot protection and selfie verification are being introduced to combat investment fraud and extortion cases reported in the country.

articles.headline: Saudi Crown Prince faces set of interlocking economic crises
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Muhammad bin Salman faces major setbacks as the war in Yemen escalates and economic targets sputter. The postponement of the 'Davos in the Desert' summit highlights regional instability. Annual foreign direct investment is currently only one-third of the $100 billion target, while the economy is expected to contract by 3.3% in 2026.

articles.headline: China tycoons face 20% tax on overseas trust gains
articles.summary: Chinese officials have begun enforcing a 20% tax on gains from overseas trusts for resident taxpayers. Eight of the world's 500 richest people could be affected, with their combined holdings totaling $140.2 billion. The move is part of President Xi Jinping's 'common prosperity' campaign as local governments search for new revenue sources.

articles.headline: Netflix replaces top creative executives amid viewership slump
articles.summary: Netflix has replaced content chief Bela Bajaria and film chief Dan Lin as the service struggles to generate major hits. Investors are concerned about stagnant US subscriber growth and competition from YouTube and TikTok. The company is experimenting with live sports and major theatrical releases to boost engagement and revenue growth.

articles.headline: Edelweiss arm India Alternatives to launch ₹1,200 crore IPO
articles.summary: EAAA India Alternatives Ltd will open its ₹1,200 crore initial public offering for subscription on October 26. The issue is entirely an offer for sale by the Edelweiss Group. The IPO size was reduced from an initial ₹1,500 crore. The company will not receive any proceeds from the offering as the entire amount goes to the selling shareholder.

articles.headline: IEA ready to coordinate further emergency oil stock releases
articles.summary: The International Energy Agency (IEA) is prepared to coordinate additional emergency oil releases if needed to cool surging prices. Disrupted supplies from the Gulf and Russia have sent diesel prices to record highs. The IEA is currently front-loading the release of 20 million barrels of diesel as part of existing emergency plans.

articles.headline: AI tool developed to predict cancer survival from facial photos
articles.summary: Researchers have built an AI tool that predicts cancer patients' survival chances using a single photograph of their face. Trained on 40 million facial images and 30,000 cancer patient records, the tool provides risk scores to identify patients likely to die within 90 days. The technology could guide treatment decisions where medical data is scarce.

articles.headline: Indian family spends under ₹8 lakh on Swiss winter trip
articles.summary: An Indian family of five managed a peak-season Swiss winter holiday for ₹7.84 lakh by using smart planning. Cost-saving measures included booking direct flights at off-peak summer rates, renting an automatic SUV to avoid expensive train passes, and cooking most meals in countryside Airbnb rentals rather than dining out.

articles.headline: Legal experts outline routes for family trademark transfers
articles.summary: Trademark disputes in family businesses can be avoided through four key legal routes: assigning the mark to a company or trust, registering heirs as joint proprietors, granting a perpetual license to one heir, or geographically dividing the mark's use. Indian law requires clear differentiation to ensure that multiple users do not deceive or confuse the public.

articles.headline: QR code technology revolutionized small merchant digital payments
articles.summary: Low-cost QR code stickers, invented by Masahiro Hara in 1994, liberated small Indian merchants from expensive point-of-sale terminals. Interoperable UPI QR codes allowed vendors to accept payments from different apps through one sticker. Today, over 65 million Indian merchants use the technology, creating sales trails that enable access to microcredit.

articles.headline: French fiscal deficit offers lessons on profligacy and restraint
articles.summary: France’s budget deficit exceeding 5% of GDP and its high debt-to-GDP ratio of 120% have led investors to view it as economically vulnerable. The situation mirrors past European crises, highlighting that as global credit gets costlier, fiscal responsibility is essential even for wealthy nations. France's bond yields reflect rising risk premia.

articles.headline: IMF warns of global economic resilience under test
articles.summary: The IMF projects global growth at 3.1% in 2026, noting that the economy has remained resilient despite multiple shocks. However, rising public debt limits fiscal stimulus options, and inflation constrains monetary policy. The report highlights a 'two-speed' global economy where AI leaders benefit while net energy importers face higher costs.

articles.headline: India's carbon market needs support beyond price signals
articles.summary: The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) marks a milestone for India, but industrial decarbonization requires more than just price signals. Experts suggest that hard-to-abate sectors need infrastructure support, affordable finance, and a finalized Climate Finance Taxonomy. Targeted incentives like Sweden’s Hybrit could serve as a model for India's green transition.

articles.headline: Interdisciplinary researchers argue global pause on frontier AI is feasible
articles.summary: A new report concludes that a global pause on training frontier AI models could be enforced by controlling the supply of specialized chips. By halting production of training-capable chips and switching to inference-only chips, regulators could restrain dangerous developments while allowing economic benefits. Monitoring concentrated supply chains is key to enforcement.

articles.headline: Technocratic fixes fail to solve Delhi's air pollution crisis
articles.summary: Satellite surveillance and mechanized seeders have failed to curb stubble burning in northern India as farmers 'game' the system. The root cause is a political economy that makes rice farming highly attractive through floor prices and subsidies. Experts argue that only a significant decline in paddy acreage near the capital will truly clear the skies.

articles.headline: Proposed legal framework suggests holding AI users liable for harm
articles.summary: As AI models move toward 'continual learning,' where weights change post-deployment, current safety evaluations may become obsolete. A proposed legal approach suggests that model developers' liability should end at the 'meter,' similar to utility companies. Users who train and deploy these models would be strictly liable for any resulting harm.

articles.headline: New AI assistants aim to act as digital chiefs of staff
articles.summary: AI personal assistants like Instinct, Muse, and Faff are integrating with WhatsApp to automate everyday administration. These 'agents' can book couriers, handle tax notices, and coordinate with vendors. While offering significant productivity gains, early users have highlighted concerns regarding data privacy, supervision requirements, and AI hallucinations.

articles.headline: Oakley Meta Vanguard smart glasses face functionality challenges
articles.summary: The Oakley Meta Vanguard smart glasses, priced at ₹52,300, offer Garmin and Strava integration but are not as autonomous as advertised. A review reveals the glasses require a constant phone connection for most smart features, effectively acting only as a camera and audio device without it. The data integration is retrospective rather than in real-time.

articles.headline: Apple Watch Series 12 offers more granular health tracking
articles.summary: The new Apple Watch Series 12 features a redesigned heart rate sensor and a readiness score to help users plan activities. The S11 chip enables faster data processing and new background health checks. While battery life remains at one day, its fast-charging capability and detailed health metrics make it a strong upgrade for owners of older models.

articles.headline: Calcutta High Court Scraps OBC Status for Several Classes in Bengal
articles.summary: The Calcutta High Court cancelled all OBC certificates issued in West Bengal after 2010. The court ruled that the identification of 77 classes as OBCs was made without proper consultation and was illegal. The order impacts thousands of beneficiaries, though those who already obtained jobs or education seats under the quota remain protected. The state government plans to appeal.

articles.headline: RBI to Transfer Record Dividend of 2.11 Lakh Crore to Government
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India board approved a record surplus transfer of Rs 2.11 lakh crore to the central government for the fiscal year 2023-24. This payout is more than double the previous year's amount and significantly exceeds the government's budgeted estimates. The windfall is expected to help the center manage its fiscal deficit and increase infrastructure spending.

articles.headline: Pune Porsche Crash: Police Probe Alleged Blood Sample Tampering by Doctors
articles.summary: Pune police are investigating allegations that a doctor at a state-run hospital swapped the blood samples of the juvenile driver with another person's to hide alcohol consumption. The minor’s father and grandfather are currently in custody for their alleged roles in the fatal crash that killed two engineers. Authorities have formed a committee to probe the conduct of hospital staff.

articles.headline: PM Modi Campaigns in Punjab and Delhi Amid High-Stakes Election Phase
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed rallies in Patiala and Delhi, focusing on national security and attacking the opposition alliance. He criticized the AAP and Congress for alleged corruption and communal politics. The PM emphasized the BJP's commitment to development in border states and welfare schemes, urging voters to support the NDA for a strong stable government.

articles.headline: IMD Issues Red Alert as Severe Heatwave Grips Northern India States
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department has issued a red alert for Delhi, Rajasthan, Punjab, and Haryana as temperatures soar above 45 degrees Celsius. In some parts of Rajasthan, the mercury touched 47 degrees. Authorities have warned of high health risks for vulnerable groups and urged citizens to stay indoors. Power demand has hit record levels across the National Capital Region.

articles.headline: Cyclone Remal: Low Pressure Area Intensifies Into Severe Cyclonic Storm
articles.summary: The IMD warned that a depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm named Remal by Friday evening. The storm is expected to make landfall between West Bengal and Bangladesh on Sunday. Heavy rainfall alerts have been issued for coastal districts, and fishing activities have been suspended in the northern Bay of Bengal.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Refuses to Stay NEET-UG 2024 Results Amid Paper Leak Claims
articles.summary: The Supreme Court declined to stay the results of the NEET-UG 2024 exam following petitions alleging paper leaks and irregularities. The court has sought a response from the National Testing Agency. The bench clarified that the admission process would proceed but remain subject to the final outcome of the case. Further hearings are scheduled for the month of July.

articles.headline: Delhi University Opens Undergraduate Admission Portal for 2024-25 Session
articles.summary: Delhi University has launched its Common Seat Allocation System (CSAS) for undergraduate admissions. Students who appeared for the CUET-UG exam can now register on the portal. The university is offering approximately 71,000 seats across 79 programs in 69 colleges. The first phase of the process involves registration, followed by preference filling for colleges and courses.

articles.headline: Israeli Forces Continue Rafah Operations as ICC Seeks Arrest Warrants
articles.summary: Israeli troops continued their offensive in Rafah despite warnings from the international community. The ICC prosecutor has requested arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Hamas leaders for alleged war crimes. Tensions remain high as diplomatic efforts for a ceasefire struggle to make progress amid a worsening humanitarian crisis in the Gaza Strip.

articles.headline: IPL 2024 Qualifier 2: Sunrisers Hyderabad Face Rajasthan Royals in Chennai
articles.summary: Sunrisers Hyderabad and Rajasthan Royals will compete tonight at the MA Chidambaram Stadium for a spot in the IPL final. Hyderabad looks to bounce back from their loss to KKR, while Rajasthan enters with confidence following their victory in the Eliminator. The winner of this clash will meet Kolkata Knight Riders in the title match scheduled for Sunday.

articles.headline: Adani Group Shares Rally After Supreme Court Conclusion on Hindenburg Probe
articles.summary: Adani Group stocks saw a sharp recovery after the Supreme Court indicated it would not interfere with SEBI's investigation into the Hindenburg allegations unless lapses were found. The court’s remarks provided relief to investors, leading to a surge in group market capitalization. The group has reiterated its focus on debt reduction and the completion of major infrastructure projects.

articles.headline: India Successfully Tests New Surface-to-Air Missile System off Odisha Coast
articles.summary: India successfully conducted a flight test of a new generation surface-to-air missile from the Integrated Test Range in Chandipur. The test met all mission objectives, tracking a high-speed aerial target with precision. The system is designed to neutralize low-altitude aerial threats and is part of the country's push for indigenous defense manufacturing capabilities.

articles.headline: Marco Rubio and S Jaishankar Discuss Energy Security and Defence Tie-ups
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met in Mumbai to discuss energy security, bilateral trade, and defense partnerships. Rubio noted that only a few items remain for a trade pact to be finalized shortly. The meeting also addressed technology cooperation and the crude oil situation in West Asia amid regional tensions.

articles.headline: Navratri Festive Sales See 20 Percent Growth for Apparel and Appliances
articles.summary: Sales of apparel, footwear, and home appliances rose by over 20% during the Navratri-Dussehra period. While unit growth was modest, value growth was driven by premiumization and price hikes. Vehicle retail sales grew by 2%, with over 1.03 million units sold, despite a high base from the previous year's post-GST rate-cut surge.

articles.headline: Government to Hold Global Roadshows to Attract Airport Investors
articles.summary: The Indian government plans promotional roadshows in international financial hubs to attract investors for its next round of airport privatization. Bidding for 11 airports, bundled into five groups, is expected to begin by December. The Airports Authority of India will offer these assets under 50-year lease agreements to maximize participation and feedback.

articles.headline: Indian States Compete with Unique Incentives to Attract Data Centre Investments
articles.summary: States including Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu are implementing tailored policies to attract data centre investments. Strategies include renewable energy incentives, independent electricity procurement, and the provision of powered land at large industrial sites. These moves address rising concerns over the significant power and water consumption required by the sector.

articles.headline: Mandatory Shelf Life Labels on Loose Sweets Disrupt Festive Season Business
articles.summary: Tighter food safety rules in states like Uttar Pradesh require manufacturing and expiry labels on loose sweets, causing concern for mithai makers. While regulators aim to ensure freshness and prevent adulteration, manufacturers argue the mandate adds significant costs and workload during the busy Diwali season. Small businesses are seeking more time for compliance.

articles.headline: Iran Preparing for Potential Attacks from Israel and United States
articles.summary: Senior Iranian officials state that Tehran is preparing for renewed military action rather than a deal to end the regional war. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi claimed Iran has deliberately stalled talks with the US to influence the upcoming midterms. Meanwhile, Russia and Iran are reportedly deepening their coordination as Moscow seeks a mediating role.

articles.headline: OpenAI Races for Fundraising Commitment Before Anthropic Public Market Debut
articles.summary: OpenAI is accelerating a funding round that could value the company at over $1.4 trillion, seeking to secure capital before rival Anthropic's expected public debut in November. Backers like SoftBank and MGX are in talks for a $30 billion round. The rapid timetable underscores the intense competition between AI labs for infrastructure capital and investor resources.

articles.headline: Russian Military Satellite Moves Dangerously Close to European Commercial Spacecraft
articles.summary: Tracking data showed a Russian military satellite, Cosmos-2612, moved within 100 metres of the ICEYE-X36, a European satellite supporting Ukraine's military. The maneuver has raised international concerns about Moscow's aggressive activities in low Earth orbit and the potential for disruption of critical space-based services used by the West.

articles.headline: West Asia Crisis a Matter of Deep Concern Says Jaishankar
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar discussed the West Asia crisis with UAE's Deputy CM Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, stressing the need for dialogue and diplomacy. He thanked the UAE for supporting the Indian community and emphasized the importance of maintaining the free flow of trade and energy amid regional instability caused by recent conflicts.

articles.headline: Upgrad Narrows FY26 Consolidated Net Loss to 131 Crore Rupees
articles.summary: Edtech firm UpGrad reported that its consolidated net loss for fiscal 2026 halved to Rs 131 crore, down from Rs 274 crore the previous year. Revenue from operations rose 7.5% to Rs 1,687 crore. The improvement was driven by lower depreciation, reduced advertising spends, and a 50% drop in IT expenses, while its consumer business turned profitable.

articles.headline: AI Led Deflation May Compress Legacy IT Revenues by Three Percent
articles.summary: Experts suggest that AI-driven productivity gains will cause a 2-3% annual revenue deflation in traditional IT services over the next two years. Clients are increasingly expecting more work for less money as AI agents handle coding and maintenance tasks. While companies like TCS see rising AI-related earnings, it may not yet fully offset the drag on legacy billing.

articles.headline: AI Infrastructure Startup Simplismart in Talks for 50 Million Dollar Funding
articles.summary: Simplismart is in discussions to raise $40-50 million at a valuation of $300-400 million, potentially tripling its value in months. The startup, which helps enterprises deploy AI models efficiently, has attracted interest from Peak XV Partners and Damac Digital. This comes as investors flock to a limited pool of Indian AI infrastructure opportunities.

articles.headline: Shapoorji Pallonji Group Pushes for 25,000 Crore Tata Sons Share Buyback
articles.summary: The SP Group has proposed that Tata Sons consider a selective capital reduction or share buyback worth Rs 25,000 crore to help the group repay its creditors. The proposal remains on the table despite regulatory uncertainty regarding the mandatory listing of Tata Sons as an upper-layer NBFC. The funds would be ring-fenced for the debt-laden conglomerate's repayment.

articles.headline: State Run Banks Plan New Products for Youth to Boost Engagement
articles.summary: Following a directive from the Finance Ministry, public sector banks are preparing to launch specialized savings, investment, and loan products for the youth. Features may include free demat accounts and financial planning guidance. A shared interactive portal is also being developed to build banking awareness and encourage responsible financial behavior among young citizens.

articles.headline: Highway Builders to Pay Lower Security Deposits Based on Performance Ratings
articles.summary: The Centre has linked national highway contractors' performance security deposits to their ratings, rewarding high performers with lower deposit requirements. Under the revised EPC framework, security slabs are set at 3%, 4%, and 5%. The move aims to incentivize quality construction while penalizing contractors for safety lapses, including a Rs 50 lakh fine for fatalities.

articles.headline: Brent Crude Slips After Touching Five Month High of 111 Dollars
articles.summary: Oil prices retreated after reaching a five-month high as traders balanced Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure against mediation efforts in Tehran. Brent crude futures settled around $108.72 per barrel. The market remains volatile with a significant risk premium due to threats to energy shipping routes and the ongoing conflict in West Asia.

articles.headline: Maize Supply Shortage Triggers Competition Between Poultry and Ethanol Industries
articles.summary: A drought-hit maize crop has sparked a scramble for supply among poultry feed producers, ethanol makers, and the starch industry. With maize prices rising, poultry farmers are urging the government to prioritize food and feed over fuel. Meanwhile, ethanol manufacturers face reduced incentives for maize-based fuel as the government shifts focus toward other feedstocks.

articles.headline: Festive Travel Demand Surges Despite High Airfares and Rising Hotel Rates
articles.summary: Travel bookings for the festive season remain robust, with travel firms reporting a 3-4x increase in bookings. Hotel rates are expected to rise by over 25% post-Diwali, especially in destinations like Goa and Udaipur. International bookings to Vietnam, Singapore, and Thailand are also up 80-90% year-on-year, showing no signs of slowing despite higher costs.

articles.headline: Welspun Corp Sees High Demand for Oil and Gas Pipelines in US
articles.summary: Welspun Corp expects its US manufacturing operations to thrive as the region ramps up energy infrastructure and drilling. The company has invested $350 million in two US plants and currently holds a pipeline of orders providing visibility for three years. It aims for a 35% market share in the US oil and gas pipe segment amid rising global energy prices.

articles.headline: NSE Listing Leads to Fifty Percent Drop in Unlisted Share Market
articles.summary: Trading activity in the unlisted share market has nearly halved since the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) made its stock market debut. NSE previously accounted for over 50% of the OTC market's volumes. Brokers report that while interest is emerging in other firms like Pharmeasy and Oyo, no single entity has yet matched the dominance previously held by NSE.

articles.headline: Sun Pharma to Raise 10,000 Crore Rupees for Organon Acquisition
articles.summary: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries is raising Rs 10,000 crore through rupee-denominated bonds to part-finance its $11.75 billion acquisition of Organon. The bonds, with maturities in 2031, carry coupons between 8.05% and 8.20%. Major institutional investors, including LIC and SBI Mutual Fund, are expected to participate in the debt offering to support the global expansion.

articles.headline: Elice AI IPO Crash in Seoul Stokes Concerns Over Tech Valuations
articles.summary: The 32% debut plunge of data centre developer Elice in Seoul has rattled the AI sector, fueling fears that the 'buy everything AI' era is ending. The slump follows delays in other public offerings in the sector, as soaring borrowing costs and concerns over real-world returns on AI infrastructure make investors more selective and demanding regarding neocloud valuations.

articles.headline: BARC Registration Delay Creates Divisions and Ratings Blackout for Broadcasters
articles.summary: A delay in renewing the registration of the Broadcast Audience Research Council (BARC) India is straining the television industry. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting is reviewing ownership structures and cross-media measurement progress. The resulting ratings blackout is impacting ad sales and channel evaluations, with reports of some broadcasters halting payments to BARC.

articles.headline: Schaeffler India MD Gopal Kadam Taken into Custody Following Factory Deaths
articles.summary: Schaeffler India CEO and MD Harsha Gopal Kadam was taken into custody after an investigation into a June accident at the company's Pune factory that killed two workers. The accident involved a carbon dioxide gas discharge during a cylinder replacement. The company stated it is cooperating with authorities and that day-to-day operations continue as usual.

articles.headline: Indian Branded Residences Market Predicted to Double by Year 2032
articles.summary: The market for branded residences in India is expected to double by 2032, driven by high demand from ultra-wealthy individuals. According to a Savills report, nearly 25 such ultra-luxury projects, developed in association with global hospitality or design brands, are slated for completion. These residences offer hotel-like services and premium amenities to residents.

articles.headline: JPMorgan Forecasts Bitcoin Returns of Ten Percent Over Next Decade
articles.summary: JPMorgan Asset Management has included Bitcoin in its long-term assumptions for the first time, projecting 10% annual returns. However, the firm warned of high volatility, estimated at 55%, which could undermine risk-adjusted appeal. The report noted that while Bitcoin could outperform traditional assets, its unstable correlations make it difficult to include in main portfolios.

articles.headline: New OTT Players Target Niche Audiences to Navigate Intense Market Competition
articles.summary: Fresh OTT entrants like Tiger TV and Brew TV are launching in India to target niche audiences and connected TV users. As linear television's share of ad spend declines, these platforms are focusing on specialized content like independent films or microdramas. However, low average revenue per user (ARPU) remains a significant challenge for sustainability in a market of over 50 platforms.

articles.headline: Indian Box Office Reports Seventeen Percent Growth in Cumulative Collections
articles.summary: Cumulative Indian box-office collections rose 17% to Rs 11,000 crore in the first nine months of 2026. Experts cite a 'revival of range' as films across languages and budgets find success through authentic storytelling. Regional cinema and Hollywood hits are gaining significant ground, with theatrical footfalls increasing by 5% year-on-year.

articles.headline: Gold Prices Decline as Inflation Worries Impact Federal Reserve Rate Outlook
articles.summary: Gold traded lower at around $4,120 an ounce as high oil prices fueled inflation concerns and influenced expectations for US interest rates. Higher borrowing costs generally decrease the appeal of non-interest-bearing bullion. While tech stocks saw a rebound, the yellow metal has remained under pressure amid shifting investor sentiments toward safer haven assets.

articles.headline: Congress Demands Resignation of CEC Over Alleged Poll Process Manipulations
articles.summary: The Congress party has called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging legal and constitutional violations via the ECINET portal. The party claims the portal centralizes manipulations of the poll process. Meanwhile, the government and opposition remain at odds over the timeline for consultations regarding new delimitation proposals.

articles.headline: Mamata Banerjee Accuses Central Authorities of State Sponsored Terrorism in Bengal
articles.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee has alleged 'state-sponsored terrorism' by central authorities following the detention of CJP leaders. She demanded their immediate release, claiming they were subjected to torture. This comes as the Calcutta High Court ordered a retired judge-led commission to investigate the Chorbagan stampede that claimed 19 lives.

articles.headline: China Military Monitors US Warship Near Disputed South China Sea Shoal
articles.summary: China's military deployed forces to track the USS Charleston, claiming the vessel illegally entered waters near a disputed shoal in the South China Sea. Beijing continues to assert sovereignty over most of the waterway despite competing claims from several Southeast Asian nations. Tensions have notably increased recently between Beijing and Manila over regional control.

articles.headline: Worker killed during illegal wild boar hunt in SGNP
articles.summary: A 60-year-old municipal sanitation worker was accidentally shot dead during an illegal wild boar hunt inside Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Mumbai. Two others were injured. Police arrested four, including a doctor accused of concealing the death and arranging cremation.

articles.headline: HC junks CIC order on PMs’ foreign trips citing national security
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court set aside a CIC order directing the IAF to disclose flight records for PM Narendra Modi and former PM Manmohan Singh's foreign visits. The court cited national security concerns, potential compromise of the PM's safety, and the confidential nature of the records.

articles.headline: Char Dham shrines record highest ever footfall with 56 lakh pilgrims
articles.summary: Uttarakhand's Char Dham shrines recorded a record 56 lakh pilgrim visits this year, surpassing the previous high of 52 lakh in 2023. Badrinath saw 20.6 lakh, Kedarnath 17.6 lakh, Gangotri 9.4 lakh, and Yamunotri 8.3 lakh footfall. Winter closure dates are between November 10-16.

articles.headline: Ladakh LG clears hill councils for all eight districts
articles.summary: Ladakh will extend its autonomous hill council system to all eight districts under a presidential regulation notified by LG Vinai Kumar Saxena. This expands the framework previously covering only Leh and Kargil, enabling creation of LAHDCs in all reorganized districts.

articles.headline: Desert fox kills captive-bred Great Indian Bustard in Jaisalmer
articles.summary: An experimental release of captive-bred Great Indian Bustards (GIB) suffered a setback when a desert fox killed a six-month-old male bird at Desert National Park in Jaisalmer. The bird was released last Wednesday and was attacked while drinking water.

articles.headline: BJP slams TN govt parole for 1998 Coimbatore blasts convicts
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu government's 60-day parole for five convicts in the 1998 Coimbatore serial bomb blasts has triggered backlash from BJP, accusing CM C Joseph Vijay's TVK of 'minority appeasement' and demanding immediate cancellation of parole.

articles.headline: Gratuity can’t be withheld for pending criminal proceedings: Gujarat HC
articles.summary: Gujarat High Court ruled that gratuity cannot be withheld due to pending criminal proceedings, ordering the release of the retirement benefit to a retired Arvalli district panchayat employee. The court noted no departmental inquiry was initiated and the case wasn't related to his job.

articles.headline: Ladakh’s first medical college gets health ministry approval
articles.summary: The Health Ministry has approved the operationalization of Ladakh’s first medical college in Leh, with courses set to begin in 2027–28. SNM Hospital will provide clinical training for the new institution.

articles.headline: Influencer dies by suicide after alleged cyberbullying
articles.summary: V Harish, a 27-year-old financial consultant and social media influencer with 1.3 million followers, died by suicide in Chennai after alleged cyberbullying, defamatory posts, and repeated blocking of his online channels. His father filed a complaint against another influencer, Jason Samuel.

articles.headline: BTech grad awarded ₹3Cr compensation for lost limb
articles.summary: Mumbai's Motor Accident Claims Tribunal directed a bus owner and National Insurance Co Ltd to jointly pay Snehal Zanjurne almost ₹3 crore for the loss of her right upper limb in a 2019 accident. The tribunal stated her completing BTech did not compensate for her disability.

articles.headline: India & US to boost defence, energy ties; trade deal close
articles.summary: Foreign Minister S Jaishankar met US counterpart Marco Rubio in Mumbai, agreeing to expand cooperation in energy, defence, and technology, and committing to an early trade deal. Rubio emphasized US role in diversifying India's supplies, while Jaishankar noted discussions on people-to-people ties.

articles.headline: Modi calls for unity against forces dividing India
articles.summary: PM Narendra Modi urged all political parties and national institutions to unite against forces seeking to divide society, undermine India’s dignity, and attack its culture. Speaking at Vijayadashami celebrations, he stressed national self-respect and faith in India's strength for progress.

articles.headline: Punjab CM Mann 'detained for 3 hours' at Delhi airport
articles.summary: AAP claimed Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann was detained for three hours at IGI Airport on October 19 and fined ₹50,000 upon returning from Paris. AAP media in-charge Baltej Pannu called it the Centre's attempt to 'humiliate' Mann. SAD alleged questioning over excess luggage/money.

articles.headline: Das, Ranka move HC against judicial custody; cases to Crime Branch
articles.summary: CJP's Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka approached Delhi HC challenging their judicial custody, a day before their executive magistrate hearing. They were detained Oct 13 for climbing a gate at Jantar Mantar to protest. Police transferred their cases to Crime Branch.

articles.headline: JNU students end 17-day hunger strike after admin assurances
articles.summary: JNU Students' Union called off its 17-day hunger strike after the administration agreed to address demands including revoking rustication of union office-bearers, withdrawing FIRs against students, and reviewing the controversial chief proctor’s office manual.

articles.headline: Rubio defends US ties with Pakistan amid India concerns
articles.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended US ties with Pakistan, stating the US needs relationships with countries, even those with disagreements. He said such engagement could help discourage issues India is worried about, and confirmed the next Quad summit in Manila.

articles.headline: US in talks with RIL to refine Venezuelan crude
articles.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US is discussing with Reliance Industries to increase refining capacity for Venezuelan crude. Calling India a refining superpower, he acknowledged India's need to diversify oil imports and saw Venezuela as a potential supply source.

articles.headline: 10-year-old girl charged with toddler's murder in Mumbai
articles.summary: Mumbai police registered a murder FIR against a 10-year-old girl for allegedly pushing an 18-month-old toddler from the sixth floor of a building. The girl was released to her parents, as law dictates kids aged 7-12 are exempt from prosecution unless deemed to understand actions' consequences.

articles.headline: India's smartphone sales plunge 26% in July-Sept quarter
articles.summary: India’s smartphone market suffered its steepest contraction in several quarters, with shipments plunging 26% in July-Sept. Higher prices deterred upgrades, and companies curbed supplies. Samsung displaced Vivo at the top, while Chinese brands' combined share slipped to 68%.

articles.headline: Delhi's air quality likely to worsen to 'poor' category today
articles.summary: Delhi's air quality remained 'moderate' at 183 (6pm) Tuesday, but is expected to worsen to 'poor' range Wednesday, potentially reaching 13.3% PM2.5 contribution from stubble burning by Thursday due to changing wind direction. Harvest patterns and fewer western disturbances could exacerbate the situation.

articles.headline: Delhi govt winter action plan starts Nov 1 to curb pollution
articles.summary: Delhi's winter action plan, effective Nov 1 to Feb 28, includes banning BS-VI non-Delhi registered vehicles, mandatory PUCC, 50% work-from-home emphasis, and AI monitoring of construction dust. Demolition bans are from Dec 10-Jan 20. Staggered office timings are also introduced.

articles.headline: Delhi government pulls up officials for skipping CM meetings
articles.summary: Delhi government has seriously viewed officials skipping meetings called by the chief minister, especially if decisions from Centre/LG meetings weren't communicated. Departments are now directed to prioritize CM's meetings, ensure attendance, and inform CMO of unavoidable absences. HoDs will be accountable for overdue grievance resolution.

articles.headline: Sabarmati riverfront model replicated along Yamuna in Delhi
articles.summary: Delhi government has initiated plans to replicate Ahmedabad’s Sabarmati riverfront model along the Yamuna, with the first phase from Palla to Wazirabad expected to complete in its current term. The project aims for dedicated zones for recreation and improved riverbank access, alongside Yamuna clean-up efforts.

articles.headline: 645-vehicle multilevel parking at Bhikaji Cama to open in November
articles.summary: DDA has completed a 645-vehicle multilevel parking facility at Bhikaji Cama Place District Centre, scheduled for inauguration in the first week of November. The ₹40-crore project aims to alleviate parking shortages and congestion in the commercial hub, offering EV charging and accessibility features.

articles.headline: Two injured after falling from mixer ride at Vikaspuri fair
articles.summary: Two people were injured after falling from a moving 'mixer' ride at a fair in west Delhi’s Vikaspuri Dussehra Ground. Preliminary probe suggests the ride’s gate may have broken. Fair organiser claimed they lost balance; police are investigating.

articles.headline: 125 C&D waste centres operational for pollution season in Delhi
articles.summary: To curb illegal dumping of construction and demolition (C&D) waste, MCD has operationalized all 125 secondary C&D waste collection centres. Up to 20 metric tonnes of malba can be deposited free, and 12 new truck-mounted multipurpose vehicles with anti-smog guns have been deployed.

articles.headline: Over 200 arrested in less than 2 years for employee-related thefts
articles.summary: In Delhi, 208 people have been arrested in 173 cases of employee-related thefts in 20 months, with 69 arrests this year. Trusted employees, often hired without verification, are increasingly betraying employers, sometimes in coordination with organized gangs who exploit their access to homes and valuables.

articles.headline: CM Rekha Gupta calls for unity against anti-national elements
articles.summary: Chief Minister Rekha Gupta called upon people to unite against social evil and anti-national elements, following Lord Ram's ideals. Speaking at Vijayadashami celebrations in Dwarka, she stressed eliminating hatred to build a brighter future for the country, condemning corruption and social discrimination.

articles.headline: IGNCA campus, Yamuna riverfront garden plans languish
articles.summary: Plans to build a new campus for Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) near Jamnagar House and develop Nav Bharat Udyan along the Yamuna remain stalled. Despite Central Vista redevelopment progress, both projects have seen little movement for years, with IGNCA still functioning from Hotel Janpath.

articles.headline: Toddler dies after falling from scooter in north Delhi
articles.summary: An 18-month-old boy died after falling from a scooter following a collision with a three-wheeled cargo vehicle in north Delhi’s Derawal Nagar. The boy suffered serious head injuries. Police arrested the cargo vehicle driver, Girish, for rash driving and causing death by negligence.

articles.headline: Dussehra celebrations carry messages on pollution, women’s safety
articles.summary: Dussehra celebrations in Delhi, attended by PM Modi and President Murmu, saw towering Ravana effigies burn amid fireworks. Organizers integrated messages on contemporary issues like air pollution, traffic congestion, counterfeit medicines, and women's safety, interpreting the tradition as an ongoing battle against modern evils.

articles.headline: NDMC proposes 30% property tax rebate for self-occupied houses
articles.summary: NDMC has proposed a draft introducing the unit area method for property tax, including a 30% rebate for self-occupied residential properties (up to 100 sqm) for men over 65, and all women and persons with disabilities. The public has until Oct 23 to provide feedback.

articles.headline: CJP founder Dipke urges supporters to spend time with families
articles.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke urged supporters to prioritize family during the festive season, acknowledging the toll of prolonged protests. He rejected comparisons with foreign agitations, emphasizing CJP's movement is rooted in Mahatma Gandhi’s principles of peace and non-violence.

articles.headline: Two-day remand violates legal procedure: Das, Ranka petition HC
articles.summary: CJP's Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka petitioned Delhi HC, arguing their two-day remand violated legal procedure and Right to Liberty, as their sureties were rejected. They claim their restriction is for 'public order' at a denotified protest site, which is only a regulatory issue, not a threat.

articles.headline: Two women electrocuted by snapped power cable in Ghaziabad
articles.summary: A 50-year-old woman and her 20-year-old daughter-in-law were electrocuted in Ghaziabad after coming into contact with a snapped power cable in a field. An 18-year-old daughter suffered injuries. Police said an earthmover struck an electric pole, causing a wire to snap and fall.

articles.headline: No relief for 'predatory' rape convict; attacked undertrials in jail
articles.summary: A Delhi court refused leniency to Shamshad, a 50-year-old man convicted of repeatedly sexually assaulting a 13-year-old boy, citing his 'predatory instincts' and continued sexual misconduct with undertrials in jail. He was sentenced under Pocso Act and IPC.

articles.headline: Woman stabbed to death after son’s altercation in Najafgarh
