articles.summary: A woman died after being stabbed in southwest Delhi’s Najafgarh in an attack on her and her husband, allegedly linked to an earlier altercation involving their son. The accused, Satish Lamba, has been arrested. The incident occurred when the couple went to check on their son.

articles.headline: Multiple shots fired at businessman’s factory in outer Delhi
articles.summary: Multiple rounds were fired at a businessman’s factory and a parked vehicle in outer Delhi’s Pooth Khurd. Two bike-borne, helmet-wearing persons opened fire and fled. While sources suspect a link to an alleged ₹5-crore extortion demand by a foreign-based gangster, police have not confirmed it.

articles.headline: Imphal valley shuts down over three Meitei killings
articles.summary: Manipur Police identified three arrested men as cadres of Kuki National Front (N) in connection with the killing of three Meitei villagers. Following this, a Kuki tribesman was shot dead, leading to a 24-hour total shutdown and protests by tribal unity groups, condemning the killings and 'indiscriminate' arrests.

articles.headline: Zero FIR row: Raj Cong ups ante, BJP says 'mobocracy'
articles.summary: Congress members protested at Jaipur police commissionerate demanding a zero FIR for NSUI national secretary Ritu Barala's alleged assault by Delhi police. BJP accused Congress of politicizing the issue, questioning why Rajasthan should register a complaint for an incident in Delhi.

articles.headline: PM Modi: Vijaya Dashmi is victory of truth over falsehood
articles.summary: PM Narendra Modi emphasized Vijaya Dashmi as the victory of truth over falsehood, urging a collective 'Nation First' commitment. He linked national progress to cultural identity, stressing self-reliance and drawing lessons from Lord Ram's life, including compassion and inclusion.

articles.headline: 10 drown in UP and Rajasthan during Durga idol immersions
articles.summary: Six people drowned in Uttar Pradesh and four in Rajasthan during Durga idol immersions on Tuesday. Incidents included three teenagers and a man in Gonda's Tedhi river, and two cousins in Prayagraj's Tons river. In Kota, four men went missing after a boat overturned.

articles.headline: 113-year-old Durga Puja traces Delhi’s Bengali migration story
articles.summary: North Delhi’s Timarpur Durga Puja, marking its 113th year, pays tribute to the migration of Bengali settlers to Delhi (1908-1920) after the British shifted the capital. Exhibits recreate the past through images and documents, using stories of six imaginary families to depict their journey and life in the new city.

articles.headline: Gender bias quietly dismantles female leadership in India
articles.summary: McKinsey’s 2025 research found women constitute 33% of entry-level employees but only 24% of managers in India, with recruitment, attrition, and promotion being significant barriers. The report highlights how subjective narratives, lack of sponsors, and work-life balance traps hinder women's career progression, advocating for evidence-based challenges to organisational culture.

articles.headline: Mother, beau held for killing 13-year-old twins in Rajasthan
articles.summary: Twin brothers (13) were found murdered in Badesra village, Rajasthan. Police arrested their widowed mother and her paramour for allegedly conspiring the killings after the boys opposed their relationship. The 16-year-old son was also taken into custody for involvement.

articles.headline: Trash collector burns 3 puppies alive in Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: An FIR was lodged against an unidentified garbage collector in Tiruvarur, Tamil Nadu, for burning three puppies alive. CCTV footage showed the collector covering the sleeping puppies with cardboard sheets and setting them on fire. Peta India intervened, and charges were filed under animal cruelty and BNS sections.

articles.headline: Affair suspicion ends in 2 deaths in Kachchh clash
articles.summary: Two men were killed in a clash in Kachchh after a dispute linked to suspicions of an extramarital affair. The deceased were identified as Jaypalsinh Sarvaiya and Prakash Suthar. Police reported that Vijay Gadhvi, Jaypalsinh's former driver, suspected his wife had an affair with Jaypalsinh.

articles.headline: Punjab hands over Jhota murder case to CBI
articles.summary: Ahead of Home Minister Amit Shah's meeting with the families of anti-drug activists, Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann announced his government would hand over the probe into the murder of Parvinder Singh Jhota to CBI. Shah welcomed the move, urging similar action for other drug-related deaths.

articles.headline: HC: Settlement can’t override public interest in Pocso cases
articles.summary: The Punjab & Haryana High Court refused to quash a Pocso case against a man accused of making obscene gestures at two minor girls, stating that settlement between parties cannot override public interest in offences involving children.

articles.headline: Youth killed by Assam mob after road accident
articles.summary: A Class XI student died and his friend was critically injured after being assaulted by bystanders following a road accident while puja pandal-hopping at Rangia in Assam’s Kamrup district. Police have detained two persons in connection with the assault.

articles.headline: Karachi's garba nights keep Gujarati heritage alive
articles.summary: In Karachi, Pakistan, Gujarati-speaking communities keep garba alive through Navratri, weddings, and social gatherings. A new initiative aims to unite people of different religions on the dance floor, using folk songs and Bollywood hits. Despite security concerns, garba fosters unity and celebrates diversity.

articles.headline: SC slams HC for 'misplaced sympathy' in grievous hurt case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court criticized Allahabad HC for releasing two offenders in a 2003 grievous hurt case without jail time due to a long trial, calling it 'misplaced sympathy'. SC directed the accused to surrender and ordered a fresh hearing, noting the victim still requires treatment.

articles.headline: India, US & UAE discuss energy at trilateral meet
articles.summary: Union External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, UAE Deputy PM Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio held a trilateral meeting in Mumbai. They exchanged views on energy, connectivity, and contemporary developments, reaffirming commitment to advance cooperation on trade and technology.

articles.headline: Oil majors' Q3 profits expected to soar up to 158%
articles.summary: Analysts expect oil companies to post net income gains of 85-158% in Q3 2026. The US-Israel war with Iran has disrupted global oil supplies, pushing energy prices higher and boosting refining and trading income to new highs for some refiners.

articles.headline: Asean fastest growing region for Indian exports in April-Aug
articles.summary: Asean emerged as the fastest-growing region for India’s exports during April-Aug, with a 56% increase, driven by a 2.4-fold surge in oil product shipments to over $6.1 billion. In contrast, EU saw the slowest growth, with petroleum product exports falling 21%.

articles.headline: PE-VC investments shine, may exceed $39bn this year
articles.summary: Despite global economic disruptions, private equity-venture capital (PE-VC) investments in India are expected to exceed $39 billion in 2026, driven by foreign investors' growing interest in infrastructure and domestic manufacturing. Mega bets on renewable energy, telecom towers, and data centers are key highlights.

articles.headline: Smartphone shipments slip, Chinese brands lose ground
articles.summary: India's smartphone market saw a 26% plunge in shipments in Q3 2026, the lowest third-quarter volume since 2016. Samsung regained top spot, while Chinese brands' combined share fell from 75% to 68% due to higher prices, component costs, and limited affordable SKUs.

articles.headline: Hacker group claims access to 3.8 lakh SBI data entries
articles.summary: A hacker group, 'Siriusim,' claimed to obtain confidential customer information from State Bank of India, including personal details, addresses, loan applications, and supporting documents. The group purports to possess 3.8 lakh data entries and 2,722 PDF documents, sparking cybersecurity concerns in India's financial sector.

articles.headline: Hotel tariffs in Delhi, Mumbai top Rishikesh, Ranthambore
articles.summary: For the first time since Covid, Mumbai and Delhi have overtaken Rishikesh and Ranthambore with the highest average hotel tariffs in India. Hotelivate’s report shows Delhi at ₹9,811 and Mumbai at ₹9,761 RevPAR, indicating a revival in corporate, international, and MICE activity.

articles.headline: Gold extends decline as inflation weighs on Fed rate path
articles.summary: Gold declined as elevated oil prices fueled inflation concerns and clouded the outlook for the Fed Reserve's interest-rate path. Bullion traded around $4,120/oz after a 0.6% fall, with oil climbing to a five-month high after Iran's statements on the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: Student founders need support beyond classrooms: Flexible attendance, funding
articles.summary: Indian student founders need support beyond classrooms, including flexible attendance, academic breaks, equipment access, and early financial backing. Incubators, faculty, and alumni are crucial. Experts advocate for policy changes to allow students to balance degrees with building companies, noting the high cost of some startup-focused programs.

articles.headline: GCCs emerging top career choice for tech talent: Survey
articles.summary: Indian tech professionals are increasingly choosing multinational global capability centers (GCCs) for career moves, seeking hands-on AI experience and clear career paths. A Talent500 survey found 69% prefer GCCs, ahead of product companies, despite only 36% of GCC employees finding career paths very clear.

articles.headline: Why longevity experts read organs, not disease for healthy ageing
articles.summary: Longevity experts are redefining healthy aging by measuring 'intrinsic capacity' – how organs and body systems perform internally – rather than solely disease management. This approach, introduced by WHO, tracks subtle shifts in functional ability like grip strength and balance to predict organ decay and allow early lifestyle interventions for longer, healthier lives.

articles.headline: CT scans not for everyone; risks and alternatives considered
articles.summary: The article discusses the risks associated with CT scans, suggesting they are not for everyone. It encourages careful consideration and exploring alternatives where appropriate, emphasizing that while useful, their use should be balanced with potential health impacts.

articles.headline: Knee-friendly strength training for mobility and balance
articles.summary: Knee-friendly strength training involves exercises that build muscle, maintain mobility, agility, and balance, reducing fall risks. Five moves are suggested: goblet squat, step-up, jump squat, twisting jump-ups, and quick feet. These target thigh muscles, strengthen legs, and improve coordination, crucial for knee health and overall stability.

articles.headline: World's refinery damage impacts global fuel supply
articles.summary: Damage to Middle Eastern and Russian refineries has caused a global fuel shortage, with India emerging as a key swing supplier due to its increased refining capacity, ability to process various crude types, and proximity to West Asia. India exported 1.4mn barrels of refined products daily, meeting urgent global demand for fuels like diesel and jet fuel.

articles.headline: How to take research beyond the ivory tower
articles.summary: India produces vast publicly funded science, but much remains inaccessible. A new AI-powered platform, SARAL.AI, aims to translate research into accessible formats like videos and podcasts in multiple languages. Challenges remain in reach, incentives for researchers, and ensuring accuracy, highlighting the need for cultural and institutional shifts.

articles.headline: Why Ravan keeps coming back: Ego, not vices, is the source
articles.summary: Ravan's ten heads symbolize human vices, but they regenerate because the source, ego (body consciousness), remains. To defeat Ravan, one must strengthen soul consciousness—the true awareness of being an eternal soul. This inner victory replaces vices like anger, jealousy, greed, and attachment with peace, cooperation, contentment, and unconditional love.

articles.headline: Hollywood turns on tech tycoons; new films portray 'billionaire villains'
articles.summary: Hollywood is producing a swarm of films (e.g., 'Artificial,' 'Musk,' 'You Can See Everything') damning Silicon Valley billionaires like Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Elizabeth Holmes for 'godlike ambition and monstrous indifference.' This reflects growing American backlash against wealth creation and anti-establishment mood, portraying tech elites as expedient monopolists.

articles.headline: Truth be trolled: The marvels of cyberspace commentary
articles.summary: This satirical piece explores the phenomenon of online trolls, describing them as 'far-from-imaginary beings who live in cyberspace and have marvellous powers of endlessly posting comments.' It humorously depicts trolls as prioritizing their 'sensibilities' over general knowledge or common sense, and boasts about their 'high literary standards' like 'Leo Trollstoy'.

articles.headline: Doctors need armour as violence rises in Indian healthcare
articles.summary: Violence against doctors and hospital staff is a routine occupational hazard in India, with 77.3% reporting violence. Recent incidents in Mumbai suburbs highlight how grief and anger escalate, often exacerbated by overcrowding, staff shortages, communication failures, and perceived wrong treatment. Stronger laws and systemic improvements are needed to protect healthcare workers.

articles.headline: France imposes fresh curfews ahead of new weekend protests
articles.summary: France imposed fresh curfews in Paris and Lyon after destructive rioting, with PM Sébastien Lecornu planning a 'massive' security operation for Saturday's protests. Police arrested a suspect in the Limoges city hall arson, amidst calls for more 'yellow vest' demonstrations over fuel prices and socio-economic issues.

articles.headline: Trump wants 'New America' for New Mexico, reviving name debate
articles.summary: US President Trump proposed renaming New Mexico 'New America,' claiming it would boost prestige. New Mexico's reps rejected the idea, highlighting the state's historical name predates the US. The move revives debate on America's naming after Vespucci and its impact on Indigenous communities.

articles.headline: Australia to sue social media over underage users
articles.summary: Australia's government plans to sue Facebook, TikTok, and other major digital platforms for alleged non-compliance with a nationwide social media ban for under-16s. Communications Minister Anika Wells confirmed the eSafety Commissioner is investigating Meta Platforms Inc. and TikTok, Snapchat, and YouTube.

articles.headline: Altman's sister's sexual abuse lawsuit dismissed
articles.summary: Sam Altman, OpenAI co-founder, won the dismissal of a civil lawsuit from his sister, Annie Altman, accusing him of repeated sexual abuse over two decades. The US district judge dismissed the case because Annie Altman refused to appear for a medical examination despite warnings.

articles.headline: Police clash with protesters for 8th day in Albania
articles.summary: Police in Tirana, Albania, used tear gas and water cannons to disperse protesters on the eighth day of violent anti-government demonstrations demanding PM Edi Rama's resignation. Rama condemned the unrest as a 'hybrid war' exploiting legitimate concerns over the cost of living and future security.

articles.headline: 2 men rearrested in UK over alleged Iran air base plot
articles.summary: British police rearrested two men on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service in a suspected plot at a US-run air base in England. The men, a 24-year-old British national and a 25-year-old dual UK-Iranian national, were arrested under the National Security Act.

articles.headline: South Korea pulls embassy staff from Kyiv amid spat
articles.summary: South Korea decided to withdraw some embassy staff from Kyiv due to an escalating spat over Ukraine's disclosure of transferring North Korean POWs to the South. Seoul demanded a public apology from Kyiv for allegedly violating a confidentiality agreement and cited persistent airstrike threats.

articles.headline: Portuguese police clear housing protest camps, make 55 arrests
articles.summary: Portuguese police cleared protest camps in Lisbon and Porto, removing activists who had occupied two squares to protest against a worsening housing crisis. A total of 55 arrests were made during the operations.

articles.headline: Australian lawmaker loses leg after being hit twice by vehicle
articles.summary: Doctors amputated the leg of Australian lawmaker Helen Haines after a man rammed her with his car and then reversed to hit her a second time. The incident, being investigated as targeted by anti-terrorism police, was linked by PM Anthony Albanese to a climate of 'ugly, polarised political debate.'

articles.headline: Tarique Rahman warns of unrest by '2 united parties' in Bangladesh
articles.summary: PM Tarique Rahman alleged that the deposed authoritarian regime and another party operating in Bangladesh have united to create unrest. He apparently referred to the banned Sheikh Hasina-led Awami League and hardline Jamaat-e-Islami, urging people to remain alert to attempts to destabilize the country.

articles.headline: Two British Indians assaulted during festival celebrations in UK
articles.summary: Two Telugu Hindu men were assaulted during a Dussehra and Bathukamma celebration in Ossett, West Yorkshire, in what police believe was a racially aggravated attack. A group of 8-10 youths, some in balaclavas, confronted them with aggressive language and physically assaulted them.

articles.headline: Bela Bajaria leaves Netflix after giving global blockbusters
articles.summary: Bela Bajaria is leaving Netflix as chief content officer, replaced by Peter Rice. Her departure comes amid pressure for Netflix to produce bigger hits and sustain viewer engagement. Bajaria, the first Indian to head a major studio, oversaw global hits like Squid Game and Bridgerton, and expanded Indian-language content.

articles.headline: Gritty Himachal delay Mumbai’s Ranji Trophy charge
articles.summary: Himachal Pradesh's batters showed grit on Day Three of their Ranji Trophy match against Mumbai, with opener Innesh Mahajan (37), skipper Pukhraj Mann (34*), and Vaibhav Kalta (14*) stonewalling Mumbai's charge. Himachal was 144/3, still trailing by 244 runs, after capitulating for 140 in first innings.

articles.headline: Gavaskar's prescription for NZ: Play late to counter swing
articles.summary: Sunil Gavaskar advised Indian batters to play the ball as late as possible against New Zealand in the upcoming two-Test series, where swing and seam are expected to pose a major challenge. He also questioned the scheduling of only two Tests, advocating for a minimum of three matches per series.

articles.headline: Diksha Dagar eyes final stand as injury cuts short season
articles.summary: Golfer Diksha Dagar, struggling with a knee injury for five months, will play the $500,000 Hero Women’s Indian Open as her final event this season. Despite the setback, she remains motivated, aiming to finish well and leveraging her strong short game.

articles.headline: Tsitsipas lets go of father-coach to rediscover his game
articles.summary: Stefanos Tsitsipas acknowledged that ending his professional relationship with his father, Apostolos, as his coach helped him regain his bite in tennis. The Greek star, once ranked No. 3, believes he's playing better tennis now that he has room to breathe and experiment, free from the pressure and tension.

articles.headline: Bayern face Arsenal examination in Champions League
articles.summary: Champions League hopefuls Bayern Munich will face an early test against English champions Arsenal on Wednesday without in-form winger Michael Olise, who is suspended. Bayern will rely on Harry Kane, with Jamal Musiala struggling and other wingers not in best form.

articles.headline: Mourinho warns no 'untouchable' stars at Real Madrid
articles.summary: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho warned Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior and other stars that no one is 'untouchable.' Mourinho emphasized that a player's performance on the pitch, not status or years at the club, makes them untouchable, amid Vinicius's struggle for form.

articles.headline: EFI administration slaps defamation notice on rider Hriday Chheda
articles.summary: Lt Col Sandeep Dewan, member (administration) of EFI's ad-hoc committee, served a defamation notice on Asian Games gold medallist Hriday Chheda, demanding ₹25 lakh and an apology. The notice concerns allegations about the handling of the Indian dressage team ahead of the Games, raising questions about administrative priorities.

articles.headline: Khushi Kadian makes mark with three tennis titles
articles.summary: Thirteen-year-old Khushi Kadian swept the girls’ under-14 singles, under-16 singles, and under-16 doubles titles at the Fenesta Open National tennis meet. Her triple crown reflects a transformation from getting disheartened by losses to focusing on patience and working hard, with aspirations for junior Grand Slams.

articles.headline: Why AI Can’t Replace A Guru: Inner Journey Needs Master's Guidance
articles.summary: While AI can interpret scriptures and mimic empathy, it cannot guide the inner journey. A living guru offers customized paths, points out subtle flaws, and bestows right understanding. Overcoming ego, the hardest human emotion to transcend, requires Divine help, which an enlightened master provides, leading seekers to inner blossoming without being affected by their burdens.

articles.headline: Vijay Varma: My job is to investigate 'bad people' in art
articles.summary: Actor Vijay Varma believes his job is to investigate 'discarded as bad people' in his roles, stating that great drama lies in conflict and shades of grey. He sees himself as 'the face of a new kind of Bollywood,' focusing on immersive storytelling that captivates audiences, reflecting a shift from traditional films.

articles.headline: Restored 'Pakeezah' closes BFI London Film Festival with sold-out show
articles.summary: Kamal Amrohi’s restored classic 'Pakeezah' made a sold-out debut at the BFI London Film Festival, chosen as the closing gala. Tajdar Amrohi, the director's son, expressed overwhelming emotion, stating it was 'almost a miracle' to see the film return to the big screen after a challenging two-year restoration process.

articles.headline: Burna Boy, Karan Aujla to headline Rolling Loud India 2026
articles.summary: Hip-hop heavyweights Burna Boy, Metro Boomin, and Skepta will make their Indian debuts headlining Rolling Loud India 2026. The two-day festival, taking place on December 12 and 13, features a stacked roster anchored by Karan Aujla, Big Sean, Seedhe Maut, and Dhanda Nyoliwala.

articles.headline: Why India needs to see the human side of Daler Mehndi
articles.summary: This opinion piece argues for empathy towards Daler Mehndi amid social media trolling following a recent performance, dismissing baseless drinking rumors. It highlights his immense cultural legacy and philanthropic contributions, emphasizing that artists are human and face struggles. The article urges a shift from quick judgment to respect for icons.

articles.headline: Bridal trousseau to garba glam: Reuse festive dressing
articles.summary: A newly-wed bride’s trousseau can be restyled for festive dressing. Embroidered lehengas, rich silk saris with contemporary blouses, and embellished dupattas transform simple kurta sets. Jewellery can be mixed and matched, swapping polki for oxidised silver jhumkas or layering bangles, emphasizing versatility and celebrating tradition through re-wearing.

articles.headline: Hindu College alumni celebrate lifelong college ties, revisit memories
articles.summary: Hindu College alumni reconnected at the Old Students’ Association Annual Alumni Awards, rekindling bonds and revisiting memories. Former principal Dr Kavita Sharma expressed pride in being a Hinduite. The event honored alumni achievements and celebrated the institution's stakeholders, noting the enduring spirit of Hindu College.

articles.headline: TOI Healing India Forum celebrates wellness journey leaders
articles.summary: The TOI Healing India Forum 2026 honored practitioners, professionals, and institutions contributing to holistic well-being. The event recognized 32 winners across 35 categories, including Ayurveda, energy healing, meditation, and yoga, highlighting the blend of ancient knowledge with modern wellness practices.

articles.headline: Heritage jewellery finds favour with Gen Z shoppers
articles.summary: Gen Z customers are embracing heritage jewellery, seeking traditional designs in lighter, more contemporary forms. Minimalist polki and kundan necklaces, jhumkas, and bangles are popular versatile pieces. Experts advise checking craftsmanship and purity for Kutchi silver and hallmarking for gold.

articles.headline: Jennifer Lopez, Brett Goldstein spark real-life romance buzz
articles.summary: Jennifer Lopez and Brett Goldstein are reportedly dating, with sources confirming their off-screen chemistry from their recent rom-com, 'Office Romance.' Speculation intensified after they were spotted arriving separately but leaving in the same car from a talent manager’s party in Los Angeles.

articles.headline: Gwyneth Paltrow returns to TV with thriller 'The Apology'
articles.summary: Oscar-winning actor Gwyneth Paltrow is set to lead 'The Apology,' a thriller drama that received a two-season straight-to-series order. Paltrow will play Evelyn Amspoker, whose son was murdered 18 years earlier. This marks her first major lead role in a television series.

articles.headline: Selena Gomez opens up on struggle with vaping, voice change
articles.summary: Selena Gomez opened up about how her prolonged nicotine vaping habit changed her voice, warning fans it's 'just not worth it.' In an Instagram Stories video, she admitted frequent vaping altered her voice and acknowledged the change might be permanent. She expressed hope to quit, calling it 'really hard.'

articles.headline: T.N. bypoll: NTK’s Dharapuram candidate Karthika arrested
articles.summary: Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) functionary M. Karthika and seven others were arrested for protesting during Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s roadshow in Dharapuram. NTK chief Seeman condemned the arrest as "fascist and retributive" politics by the TVK government, alleging false charges. DMK president M.K. Stalin also demanded her release, criticizing the TVK for misusing power.

articles.headline: Crackdown on protesters violates India’s international legal obligations: UN experts
articles.summary: UN human rights experts stated that recent actions by Indian security agencies and police in Delhi against protesters violate India’s "core international legal obligations." They expressed concern over reports of 7,000 youths, journalists, and human rights defenders detained, and excessive force used, calling for an independent investigation. The External Affairs Ministry has yet to respond.

articles.headline: Call to classify assistive devices as essential products
articles.summary: Doctors with Disabilities: Agents of Change has urged the Union government to classify augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) devices as essential assistive products under the draft Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules, 2026. The group argues this classification would ensure better access to insurance, public financing, replacement, and maintenance, reflecting their role in enabling autonomy and rights.

articles.headline: Cyclones, floods and landslides threaten telecom resilience
articles.summary: A study by the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure found telecom towers in Assam, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Odisha, and Uttarakhand highly vulnerable to natural disasters. In Tamil Nadu, 57% of towers face high cyclonic wind risk. The report recommends stronger physical protection, backup networks, and improved disaster preparedness to ensure crucial connectivity for essential services.

articles.headline: Political differences must not hinder national interest: PM Modi
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, addressing a Vijayadashami celebration in Delhi, identified "forces harming the country, those dividing society, and a mindset hostile to Indian culture" as India's enemies. He urged people and institutions to unite, prioritizing national interest over political differences, and to work towards a self-reliant, developed India.

articles.headline: SP to release manifesto on Constitution Day focusing on ‘PDA’ plan
articles.summary: The Samajwadi Party (SP) will release its 2027 Assembly poll manifesto, 'Jan-Man Manifesto', on November 26, Constitution Day. Party president Akhilesh Yadav announced it will highlight the SP’s outreach to "Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak" (PDA) communities, along with separate sections for women, youth, and law and order, reflecting a commitment to social justice.

articles.headline: China imposes restrictions on export of tunnel-boring, high-altitude machinery
articles.summary: China will introduce export controls from November 18 on tunnel-boring machines (TBMs) and heavy machinery for high-altitude terrain (above 3,000 metres) to "safeguard national security and interests." Exports to "sensitive countries and regions in dispute with China" will require a license. India has previously raised concerns about TBM import delays from China.

articles.headline: Less than 1% of Delhi Form 6s processed
articles.summary: Only 1,238 of 4.5 lakh Form 6 applications for inclusion in Delhi’s electoral roll have been processed in 42 days, with the special intensive revision (SIR) underway. This delay, ahead of the November 30 deadline, raises concerns for citizens seeking re-inclusion or first-time registration, as less than 1% of applications have been disposed of.

articles.headline: Oppn. accuses BJP govt. in Odisha of ‘silence’ on disputed region with A.P.
articles.summary: Opposition parties in Odisha accused the State BJP government of compromising territorial integrity in the disputed Kotia region with Andhra Pradesh, citing its "studied silence." This follows an Andhra Pradesh notification for rural polls in three Kotia panchayats. The BJD and Congress allege the Majhi government is in a bind due to the TDP’s support for the Central government.

articles.headline: JNUSU ends 17-day protest after rustication orders revoked
articles.summary: Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) has revoked the rustication of four students’ union office-bearers and a former president, ending their 17-day hunger strike. The university also agreed to withdraw FIRs against students, review the Chief Proctor Office manual on demonstrations, and form a committee to examine reinstating the JNUEE admission process.

articles.headline: AAP seeks FIR against Ramlila panel over cockroach effigy
articles.summary: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) filed complaints seeking an FIR against a Ramlila committee and its BJP MLA president for burning an effigy of a cockroach alongside Ravana, Meghnad, and Kumbhakarna in Delhi. AAP alleged it hurt Hindu sentiments by mocking sacred traditions, while the CJP, whose founder ignited it, called it a symbol of "filth."

articles.headline: Govt. acting early, firmly against foul air, says CM
articles.summary: Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced Delhi's Winter Action Plan will be enforced from November 1 to February 28, 2027, to combat air pollution. Measures include construction and demolition curbs, AI-based site monitoring, 50% work from home, staggered office timings, and bans on non-BS-VI Delhi registered vehicles.

articles.headline: Two hurt as amusement ride gate breaks open
articles.summary: Two people were injured after falling from a 'Mixer Ride' at a Dasara ground in west Delhi’s Vikaspuri when its gate broke open. Police registered an FIR and said organizers had all required licenses. The injured are being treated at RML Hospital.

articles.headline: Cong. plans ‘Uttarakhand Nyay Yatra’ ahead of 2027 polls
articles.summary: The Uttarakhand Congress unit unveiled its 'Uttarakhand Nyay Yatra' roadmap, aiming to reach the public ahead of the 2027 Assembly election. The yatra will highlight the BJP government’s "anti-people policies" and "pressing issues" facing the State, focusing on constituencies in Dehradun district.

articles.headline: Pinarayi questions SMA drug ‘trial’ in govt. hospital
articles.summary: Kerala Leader of Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan alleged that "experimental drugs" for clinical trials were distributed to SMA patients at SAT Hospital, marked "Physician Sample" and "For Clinical Trials Only." The hospital clarified only CDSCO-ratified drugs are used, distinguishing it as a generic version of a patented drug, approved by SAT, making it affordable.

articles.headline: BJP backs SIR of electoral rolls to keep out ‘outsiders’: Arunachal leader
articles.summary: The Arunachal Pradesh BJP unit supported the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, emphasizing accurate voter lists against "illegal migrants." State general secretary Tatar Niglar said SIR protects indigenous land, culture, and identity against numerically larger "outsiders," criticizing protests as politically motivated.

articles.headline: Congress leaders protest over alleged assault on NSUI secy.
articles.summary: Senior Congress leaders and workers staged an overnight protest at the Jaipur Police Commissionerate, demanding an FIR over the alleged assault on NSUI national secretary Ritu Barala during a recent protest in New Delhi. PCC president Govind Singh Dotasra vowed to stay until an FIR was registered, while police used mild force to disperse protesters.

articles.headline: Digvijaya Singh embarks on Ujjain to Ayodhya ‘Satya Sanatan Yatra’
articles.summary: Senior Congress leader Digvijaya Singh commenced his 'Satya Sanatan Swabhiman Yatra' from Ujjain, covering 930 km to Ayodhya. The foot march, led by seers, aims to promote Sanatan culture and traditional values, with Mr. Singh offering prayers at significant temples before starting.

articles.headline: Mirwaiz expresses concern over Race Course Mosque ‘eviction notice’
articles.summary: Chief cleric of Kashmir, Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, expressed concern over a reported eviction notice for the historic Race Course Mosque in New Delhi, a gazetted waqf property since 1977. He criticized the failure of waqf authorities to defend the mosque and warned of diminishing safeguards for other Muslim religious endowments following Waqf amendments.

articles.headline: Medical interns resume strike in J&K hospitals over stipend hike promise
articles.summary: Hundreds of medical interns in Jammu and Kashmir hospitals resumed their strike, alleging the government failed to implement a promised stipend hike from ₹12,300 to ₹30,000 despite a month-old written assurance. They criticized "humiliating remarks" from officials and vowed not to end agitation until an official government order is issued.

articles.headline: Defeat leaders who oppose Maratha quota, Jarange urges people
articles.summary: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange-Patil urged his community to defeat political leaders opposing reservation in upcoming elections, addressing a Dasara rally in Beed. He also criticized the Devendra Fadnavis government for "meagre" drought compensation for farmers and demanded swift clearance of crop insurance dues.

articles.headline: Activists seek Odisha Governor’s intervention for anti-mining protesters’ release
articles.summary: Human rights activists have appealed to the Odisha Governor to intervene and secure the release of individuals arrested for protesting bauxite mining at Sijimali hill. They allege indiscriminate arrests on false charges to stifle voices against potential livelihood loss and socio-ecological impact, and highlight tribal leader Lada Sikaka facing severe non-bailable charges.

articles.headline: Allahabad HC directive for U.P. panchayat polls puts ruling party in fix
articles.summary: The Allahabad High Court's directive to Uttar Pradesh to complete three-tier panchayat elections within three months has put the ruling BJP in a difficult position. The elections, deferred due to OBC reservation concerns, will now proceed under existing 27% OBC quota, forcing the government to conduct polls that influence grassroots politics before the 2027 Assembly election.

articles.headline: T.N. sanctions scheme for guaranteed 150-day work
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has approved ‘Vetri 150,’ a scheme offering an additional 25 days of employment with State funds to rural households completing 125 days under the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin). This initiative fulfills a Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam manifesto promise for the 2026 Assembly election.

articles.headline: Karnataka CM urges Centre to help sugar cane growers
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar urged the Union government to intervene in the sugar cane farmers' crisis, requesting a revision of the minimum selling price of sugar (unchanged since 2019) and an increase in cane-based ethanol prices. He warned against excluding cane-based ethanol from procurement, fearing adverse effects on mills and farmer payments.

articles.headline: Keralam seeks FSSAI criteria on high fat, sugar, salt food
articles.summary: The Keralam government will ask the FSSAI to finalize clear criteria for defining high fat, sugar, and salt (HFSS) foods to curb unhealthy eating habits among children. Health Minister K. Muraleedharan noted the absence of such criteria hinders efforts to regulate sales near schools and requested swift finalization of draft regulations.

articles.headline: Karnataka BJP predicts rebellion in Congress
articles.summary: Karnataka BJP State unit president B.Y. Vijayendra predicted a rebellion within the ruling Congress, claiming senior leaders and MLAs are set to revolt against Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar. He asserted that Mr. Shivakumar is "frustrated" and accused him of acting "impatiently" to remove the BJP government.

articles.headline: Caste groups line up rallies as U.P. Assembly election picks up
articles.summary: Several caste-centric social organizations in Uttar Pradesh are planning large gatherings and mobilizations ahead of the 2027 Assembly election. Groups representing Brahmin, Bhumihar, and Kushwaha communities will host programs to push for economic and social upliftment, better education, and political representation, seen as shows of strength for ticket distribution.

articles.headline: YSRCP alleges TDP stopping them from local body polls
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh YSRCP coordinator Sajjala Ramakrishna Reddy accused the TDP-led government of "attacks, intimidation" and criminal cases to force his party out of local body elections. He demanded a High Court judge inquiry into alleged police firing in Pulivendula and claimed caste certificates were delayed while candidates faced threats.

articles.headline: HC refuses to drop charge against father for minor son’s fatal accident
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court refused to discharge a Mysuru father from culpable homicide charges after his 14-year-old son caused an accident killing three. Emphasizing parental accountability, the court stated, "A parent who knowingly places the steering wheel in the hands of a child cannot always retreat behind the minority of that child, when the adventure ends in catastrophe."

articles.headline: Ladakh plan: L-G final authority over UT laws
articles.summary: The Centre's draft "Constitutional and Statutory Framework" for Ladakh proposes the Lieutenant-Governor (L-G) as the final authority on regulations made by the U.T.-level elected body. It seeks views on the body's composition, election methods, women's representation, and whether to grant Ladakh constitutional status or continue under the existing LAHDC Act, 1997.

articles.headline: Bengal CM hands over aid to stampede victims’ kin
articles.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari visited families of the 19 stampede victims from a Kolkata Durga Puja pandal, handing over ₹25 lakh ex gratia and assuring a government job for one person per family. Seven people have been arrested in connection with the tragedy, which occurred on October 17.

articles.headline: People facing ‘Ravana’ of joblessness, inflation: Cong.
articles.summary: Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra stated that people are confronting ‘Ravana’ in the form of unemployment and inflation, asserting that the party is "fighting for the truth." Attending a Ramlila event, she conveyed that the battle between truth and falsehood continues, and the party will persist in its fight.

articles.headline: Does govt. plan fresh delimitation proposal, asks Cong.
articles.summary: The Congress party questioned the government on its plans for a fresh delimitation proposal and criticized its refusal to convene an all-party meeting. Jairam Ramesh also asked if the Centre intended to revive the defeated Constitution Amendment Bill on women's reservation, which was previously rejected in the Lok Sabha.

articles.headline: Report flags ECINET feature to centrally control access
articles.summary: A civic tech initiative report highlights an ECINET feature allowing central control over access to enumeration forms State by State, and can even bar electoral registration officers (EROs) from viewing them in West Bengal. This raises concerns about centralization and potential manipulation of the electoral roll, echoing objections by Election Commissioners.

articles.headline: How conversion affects reservation
articles.summary: The Supreme Court upheld the Madras HC ruling invalidating Tamil Nadu’s order allowing converts from Backward Classes and Scheduled Castes to Islam to obtain Backward Class Muslim certificates. The article argues that conversion doesn't automatically grant new community status but emphasizes the need for evidence-based inquiry into continuing social disadvantage for converts.

articles.headline: Why Big Tech gives away open-weight AI models
articles.summary: Tech firms are releasing open-weight AI models to attract developers, challenge Chinese rivals, and strengthen their ecosystems. This strategy aims to encourage building applications around their models, generating revenue from services, computing infrastructure, and fostering network effects. For Indian businesses, these models offer an alternative to proprietary foreign AI solutions.

articles.headline: Amazon targets Nvidia’s software edge with AI tool
articles.summary: Amazon unveiled TorchNeuron, an open-source software tool enabling developers to run AI code on its Trainium2 and Trainium3 chips with minimal changes. This initiative challenges Nvidia's software dominance (CUDA platform) by making AI workloads more hardware-agnostic, reducing reliance on specific GPUs and fostering a broader developer ecosystem.

articles.headline: Iran Guards say mines halted three tankers in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Iranian Revolutionary Guards announced their naval mines halted three tankers attempting to travel the Strait of Hormuz via routes considered illegal by Tehran. The Guards claimed "three violating oil tankers were set ablaze and halted due to the explosion of mines planted by the brave sailors of the IRGC Navy."

articles.headline: Islamic State-linked militants kill at least 48 civilians in Mali
articles.summary: Islamic State-linked militants killed at least 48 civilians in eastern Mali in apparent retaliation for an attack on suspected informants by pro-government forces, including Russia’s Africa Corps. The attacks by Islamic State Sahel Province fighters occurred in at least five localities in Menaka.

articles.headline: Attack on market in Abyei region kills at least 153
articles.summary: A drone strike on a market in Abyei, a border region disputed by Sudan and South Sudan, hit a nearby fuel depot, killing at least 153 people and igniting a fire. Abyei's caretaker Information Minister blamed Sudan’s military for the attack on Amiet market.

articles.headline: Israeli fire kills at least four in Gaza Strip
articles.summary: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least four Palestinians, including a married couple and a 17-year-old, in separate incidents in the Gaza Strip. Israel states Hamas has been rearming and launching attacks; Hamas denies this, accusing Israel of undermining the Gaza peace deal.

articles.headline: China pulls out of Sri Lanka port logistics venture
articles.summary: China Merchants Port Holdings withdrew from a $392 million joint venture for a logistics hub at Colombo port. Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA) stated the decision not to proceed was due to "changes in external circumstances, commercial considerations and shareholder interests." SLPA will now seek an alternative development strategy via a PPP model.

articles.headline: Lula takes to streets as Flavio leans on Big Tech in Brazil polls
articles.summary: Millions of Lula da Silva's supporters rallied in Brazil's streets ahead of the October 25 presidential runoff, demanding public education, healthcare, and workers' rights. Opponent Flavio Bolsonaro's campaign reportedly paid a cybersecurity firm for AI-based data analysis and targeted messaging, benefiting from alleged "clear bias" from platforms like Instagram and WhatsApp.

articles.headline: Russia and Iran ‘never’ worked so closely, says Araghchi
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Russia and Iran have "never" worked so closely, with Moscow playing a mediating role in the West Asia war. He mentioned discussions covering Europe to West Asia, including Lebanon, Palestine, Ukraine, and Yemen, and emphasized expansion of economic and nuclear cooperation.

articles.headline: Asmita and Tanvi reach round of 16 in French Open badminton
articles.summary: Indian shuttlers Asmita Chaliha and Tanvi Sharma advanced to the round of 16 in the French Open badminton tournament in Paris. Chaliha beat Hang Qian Xi 21-18, 24-22, and Sharma defeated Isharani 21-12, 21-12. However, the women’s doubles pair of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand lost in the round of 32.

articles.headline: Ronaldo handed 30-day suspension by Portuguese federation
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has been handed a 30-day suspension and a $286 fine by the Portuguese football federation (FPF) for leaving the national team camp during the UEFA Nations League. The suspension takes effect from the day of the Denmark match.

articles.headline: Gavaskar wants India players to focus on Ranji Trophy
articles.summary: Sunil Gavaskar urged Indian players to prioritize the Ranji Trophy, arguing that the absence of several international players hinders assessment of emerging cricketers' "true capability." He criticized the excessive number of Test caps given due to resting seniors, stating that only injured players should miss Ranji games.

articles.headline: Powar replaces Agarkar, Ojha new chairman of selection committee
articles.summary: Ramesh Powar has replaced Ajit Agarkar in the men’s senior national selection committee, with Pragyan Ojha taking over as chairman due to having played the most Tests among reconstituted panel members. Shiv Sunder Das will complete his maximum four-year tenure as a selector by December.

articles.headline: Veteran sports scribe P. Krishnan passes away
articles.summary: P. Krishnan, former Senior Deputy Editor of Sportstar, passed away in Chennai. Krishnan, who joined The Hindu in 1980 before moving to Sportstar, was integral to the editorial desk for over three decades. He was known for his genial presence, editorial skills, and ability to craft iconic headlines, helping make Sportstar more than a workplace.

articles.headline: Athletics powers India’s show at Asian Para Games, takes medal tally to 35
articles.summary: Athletics spearheaded India’s performance at the Asian Para Games, securing five gold medals. Nishad Kumar won T47 long jump and high jump golds, Deepthi, Simran, and Pranav Soorma also claimed gold. India finished sixth in standings with 35 medals (nine gold, 11 silver) by end of Tuesday's events.

articles.headline: Dominant Iris hurtle past Railways
articles.summary: Indian Railways suffered a crushing 119-35 defeat against Japan's Denso Iris in a one-sided Group-B clash at the FIBA Women’s Basketball League Asia. Iris dominated from beyond the arc, converting five three-pointers in the first quarter and exposing Railways’ struggles with wayward passes, erratic shooting, and weak defense.

articles.headline: Molineux, Dunkley set ₹50 lakh base price for WPL auction
articles.summary: Australia captain Sophie Molineux and English opener Sophia Dunkley are among 27 overseas players with a maximum base price of ₹50 lakh for the Women's Premier League (WPL) mini-auction. A total of 146 players, including 119 Indians, are listed for 27 available slots across five franchises, with UP Warriorz holding the biggest purse.

articles.headline: Hingrajia leads Gujarat’s sturdy reply after Badoni’s double
articles.summary: Manan Hingrajia's unbeaten 108 led Gujarat to a sturdy 363 for five at stumps on Day Two, replying to Delhi's 648 for six declared, which was propelled by Ayush Badoni's 217. Hingrajia, along with Jaymeet Patel (72) and Chintan Gaja (41*), offered admirable restraint against Delhi's bowlers, who still hold a 285-run lead.

articles.headline: Australian umpire Treloar officiates Ranji match
articles.summary: Australian umpire Simon Treloar is officiating a Ranji Trophy match between Delhi and Gujarat as part of an exchange program between Cricket Australia and the BCCI. Treloar, an experienced umpire from New South Wales, will also officiate a match in Mumbai later this month.

articles.headline: Veteran Shami not giving up hope
articles.summary: Veteran Indian pacer Mohammed Shami expressed that he isn't giving up hope on making a return to the Indian Test team despite recent injuries. He said he’s still working hard, focusing on a comeback, and feels "young enough" to continue playing for the country.

articles.headline: Arrived wins Golconda St. Leger, dies shortly after
articles.summary: The horse Arrived won the Golconda St. Leger in Hyderabad but tragically died shortly after the race, casting a pall of gloom over the event. S. Srinivas Reddy trained the winner.

articles.headline: Punjab salvages a point against Mumbai City FC
articles.summary: Punjab FC salvaged a point against Mumbai City FC with a 1-1 draw in their ISL match. Wilmar Jordan scored for Punjab from a penalty kick after his initial attempt was saved, while Mumbai City’s Leandro Otormin scored their only goal.

articles.headline: Chacarra relied on short game to win DP World India Championship
articles.summary: Eugenio Chacarra, winner of the DP World India Championship, expressed pride in his victory despite a broken toe and physical discomfort. He highlighted his reliance on a strong short game and patience, and his ambition to join Ryder Cup stars and Spanish greats like Seve Ballesteros and Jon Rahm. He also spoke fondly of India and its people.

articles.headline: Scientists unearth new instance of ‘contagious cancer’ in animals
articles.summary: Researchers at the University of Vermont documented a fourth instance of naturally occurring contagious cancer, studying melanoma in brown bullhead catfish in Lake Memphremagog. Their findings suggest cancer cells can spread between fish, rather than arising independently, and offer clues to how foreign cells evade immune rejection, relevant to organ transplantation.

articles.headline: Bishnoi Gang Firing at Tiger Shroff's Car Spurs Bollywood Security Surge
articles.summary: Mumbai police heightened security for stars like Tiger Shroff and Salman Khan after the Lawrence Bishnoi gang fired at Shroff's car. Police believe Salman was the real target, but shifted focus to low-security Shroff, having previously issued threats, aiming to create fear. Celebrities cancelled appearances, sought bulletproof vehicles, and private security inquiries surged.

articles.headline: Rajkummar Rao Joins Sourav Ganguly for Kolkata Durga Puja Celebrations
articles.summary: Actor Rajkummar Rao, set to portray Sourav Ganguly in an upcoming biopic, celebrated Maha Ashtami and pandal-hopped with Ganguly and his family in Kolkata. Rao participated in traditional rituals, including playing the dhak, and was fascinated by the festive lights, colors, and food during his Navratri fast. Ganguly reminisced about childhood joy and family memories.

articles.headline: Entertainment Industry Defends Daler Mehndi Amidst Performance Controversy
articles.summary: Daler Mehndi faces allegations of poor performance or intoxication at a Uttarakhand event. Industry peers, including Mika Singh, Kapil Sharma, and Shaan, defended him. Mika clarified Mehndi was unwell, had heart treatment, and challenged anyone to prove Daler drinks alcohol, offering to quit singing. Supporters urged kindness and respect for his legacy.

articles.headline: Deepthi Jeevanji, Nishad Kumar Win Gold with Records at Asian Para Games
articles.summary: Indian para-athlete Deepthi Jeevanji won gold in women's 400m T20 at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya, setting a new record of 56.36 seconds. Nishad Kumar also secured gold in the high jump with a Games record. India's athletics contingent won 5 golds among 20 medals, contributing to the nation's total of 35 medals by Day 2.

articles.headline: K-Pop Star Ejae Marries Samuel Kim in Traditional Seoul Ceremony
articles.summary: KPop Demon Hunters star Ejae (Kim Eun-jae) married music producer Samuel Kim on October 17 in Seoul, South Korea. The traditional Korean Paebaek ceremony and welcome party took place at her grandparents' residence, also mentioned as Stage 28, a place linked to Ejae's childhood memories. The couple met in 2017 during a songwriting session and got engaged in Autumn 2023.

articles.headline: Jio Platforms IPO Aims to Raise ₹30,188 Crore to Eliminate Debt
articles.summary: Jio Platforms MD Akash Ambani announced the upcoming IPO, priced at Rs 1,065-1,119 to raise Rs 30,188 crore, aiming to eliminate $3 billion net debt. He called it a landmark for Indian capital markets, reflecting 500M Indians' trust. Jio, with 7,220+ patents, will lead in 5G, AI, home broadband, and explore satellite constellations, using 30% free cash flow for growth. The anchor book was oversubscribed 30 times.

articles.headline: US Secretary Rubio Discusses India's Refining Power, Venezuela Oil, FTA
articles.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, during his Mumbai visit, praised India as a "refining superpower." He discussed potential Indian oil purchases and refining Venezuelan oil at Reliance Energy's Jamnagar plant to diversify supply chains. Rubio also indicated that US-India free trade agreement negotiations are "very, very close" to completion, emphasizing energy trade's transformative role.

articles.headline: Stellantis India Targets Halving Vehicle Development Time by 2030
articles.summary: Stellantis India, under its FaSTLAne 2030 roadmap, aims to halve vehicle development time from 48 to 24 months. MD Shailesh Hazela confirmed plans to launch 12 new products across Citroen and Jeep brands while increasing local parts sourcing. Citroen already boasts 90-95% localization, with Jeep at 70-75%.

articles.headline: Coca-Cola Bottler SLMG Beverages Targets ₹20,000 Crore Turnover, IPO
articles.summary: SLMG Beverages, Coca-Cola's largest Indian bottler, plans to achieve a ₹20,000 crore turnover within five years and aims for a stock exchange listing before 2030. Joint MD Paritosh Ladhani confirmed overseas expansion is being explored. The company has invested ₹1,200 crore in its Bihar facility and another ₹1,000 crore in a new Gorakhpur, UP plant.

articles.headline: OYO Parent PRISM Halves IPO Size to ₹3,350 Crore Amid Stronger Balance Sheet
articles.summary: OYO parent PRISM (Oravel Stays) plans to halve its IPO fresh issue size from ₹6,650 crore to ₹3,350 crore. The reduction follows improved cash generation, a stronger balance sheet, and a focus on debt reduction, with most proceeds aimed at repaying existing borrowings. Moody's recently upgraded the company's outlook to 'Positive,' citing improved EBITDA and cash flow generation.

articles.headline: Cognizant, Google Cloud Expand Partnership to Accelerate Agentic AI Adoption
articles.summary: Cognizant and Google Cloud expanded their partnership to accelerate agentic AI adoption with a new 'Gemini Frontier Capability Group.' This joint investment combines Google's AI platform with Cognizant's engineering expertise and over 18,000 dedicated associates. Building on their 2026 Gemini practice, the initiative aims to provide enterprise-ready AI builders for advanced AI solutions.

articles.headline: UK Regulators Pressure Apple to Open Contactless Payments, Lower Fees
articles.summary: The UK's Competition and Markets Authority is probing Apple's mobile ecosystem dominance, considering forcing it to open iPhone contactless NFC technology to rival digital wallets. Regulators aim to foster competition by requiring Apple to lower fees and remove technical barriers, citing concerns that Apple's control blocks competition and results in high fees for other payment services.

articles.headline: IAF Chief Amar Preet Singh Completes Final Sortie Before Retirement
articles.summary: Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh completed his 55-minute final service sortie in an HJT-16 Kiran trainer aircraft at the Air Force Academy in Telangana, accompanied by his first flying instructor, Wing D Commander V S Kochar (retd). He is set to retire on October 31 after four decades of service, with Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit designated as his successor.

articles.headline: Newsprint Makers Seek PM's Intervention Over Disruptions in Coal Supply
articles.summary: The Indian Newsprint Manufacturers Association (INMA) urged PM Modi to intervene over persistent irregular coal supply from Coal India subsidiaries, despite long-term agreements. Inadequate coal rakes are disrupting newsprint production, forcing mills to buy expensive open-market coal and grid power, raising operational costs and threatening domestic print media supplies.

articles.headline: India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement Takes Effect, Boosting Trade
articles.summary: The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement, signed on April 27, became operational on Tuesday, marking India's 17th FTA. It grants duty-free access for Indian goods, especially in textiles and leather. New Zealand PM Christopher Luxon stated it enables Kiwi businesses to reach over a billion customers with reduced tariffs and committed $20 billion FDI over 15 years.

articles.headline: RSS Chief Warns Against Regime-Change Agitations, External Manipulation
articles.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, during his Vijayadashami speech in Nagpur, warned that regime-change agitations do not solve problems and could be exploited by global powers seeking to destabilize India. Citing examples from Bangladesh, France, Albania, and Nepal, he urged citizens to remain united, prevent deepening social divisions, and resist external attempts to create anarchy, stressing protests should resolve issues.

articles.headline: Calcutta HC Orders Retired Judge to Lead Kolkata Stampede Inquiry
articles.summary: The Calcutta High Court ordered the West Bengal government to form a judicial commission, led by a retired High Court judge, to investigate the October 17 Durga Puja pandal stampede in Chorbagan TVK that killed 19. The panel, which will exclude Kolkata police and KMC officials, will examine lapses by organizers, police, civic body, and fire department.

articles.headline: Centre Reviews 2019 National Mineral Policy for Critical Minerals, Deep Sea Resources
articles.summary: The Union Mines Ministry is reviewing the National Mineral Policy, 2019, forming a nine-member committee chaired by the additional secretary. The committee will recommend comprehensive revisions within two months, focusing on critical minerals, deep-sea resources, and recycling. The aim is to align India's mineral sector with evolving global requirements, domestic industrial demand, and sustainability goals.

articles.headline: CBDT Introduces Form 173A for Gsecs Tax Exemption Claims
articles.summary: The CBDT has notified new Form 173A under Income-Tax Rules 2026, mandating detailed disclosures for claiming income-tax exemptions on interest and capital gains from government securities. Applicable to Foreign Institutional Investors and the Bank for International Settlements, taxpayers must provide transaction-level details, including ISIN numbers and holding values, to ensure transparency.

articles.headline: CJP Leaders Challenge Judicial Custody Extension in Delhi High Court
articles.summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka approached the Delhi High Court seeking an urgent hearing against the two-day extension of their judicial custody. Detained October 13 for allegedly entering Jantar Mantar unauthorized, they claim their detention is illegal, violates liberty for political reasons, and questions public order justification for protesting at a denotified site.

articles.headline: Zelenskyy Meets US Envoy Witkoff in Oslo to Repair Strained Ties
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo, hosted by Norway and Finland, to repair strained US-Ukraine relations. Amid Kyiv's complaints of withheld defense support and concerns over the Trump administration's stance toward Moscow, the meeting aimed to secure vital military aid, with Zelensky also requesting Kyiv's representation in any US-Russia-China talks. Washington denies deliberately hindering Ukraine's war effort.

articles.headline: Houthi Missile Strike Kills 73 Recruits in Yemen, Escalating Conflict
articles.summary: A Houthi ballistic missile strike on Yemen's al-Alam training camp in Shabwa province killed 73 new recruits (aged 18-20) and wounded over 200, making it the deadliest attack in three months and shattering a 2022 ceasefire. Another Houthi missile killed two teenage girls in Taiz. Britain announced increased military support for Saudi Arabia against the Houthis.

articles.headline: Hindusthan National Glass Plans ₹500 Crore Capacity Expansion
articles.summary: Hindusthan National Glass, now under the Madhvani-Turner Group after a ₹2,250 crore acquisition through insolvency, plans to invest up to ₹500 crore over five months to expand its manufacturing capacity. Having already added over 1,100 tonnes per day of capacity since the takeover, the company expects to return to profitability this quarter by reactivating mothballed furnaces.

articles.headline: Alberta Voters Overwhelmingly Reject Separation from Canada
articles.summary: Voters in oil-rich Alberta overwhelmingly rejected separation, with 76% supporting unity in a non-binding referendum. This provides a significant boost to Prime Minister Mark Carney's unity efforts amidst trade tensions with the US. Separatists contend Alberta subsidizes poorer Canadian regions, but only 24% backed provincial independence.

articles.headline: Rajnath Singh Urges SCO to Dismantle Terror Ecosystem, End Financing
articles.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, addressing the SCO meeting in Dushanbe with Pakistan's Deputy PM present, urged member states to firmly dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism, stressing there can be no justification or safe havens for those who finance terror. He emphasized resilient supply chains, economic cooperation, and connectivity projects respecting national sovereignty.

articles.headline: Amit Shah Vows to Eradicate Punjab Drug Trade by 2029, Slams AAP
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah, after meeting families affected by Punjab's narcotics crisis, vowed to eradicate the drug trade by December 31, 2029. He criticized the AAP government for failing its promise to solve the issue, accusing it of political patronage for the growing trade, which he noted was worse than official reports, making it a key 2027 Assembly election poll issue.

articles.headline: Mumbai Police Interrogate Three Suspects in Tiger Shroff Firing Case
articles.summary: Mumbai Police secured a 48-hour transit remand for three suspects from Haryana and Bihar, arrested in Rajasthan, regarding the firing outside actor Tiger Shroff's football practice. The accused allegedly discharged five rounds. The Mumbai Crime Branch’s Anti-Extortion Cell is investigating links to the Bishnoi gang, exploring motives of extortion or intimidation of the Bollywood actor.

articles.headline: UK RAF Typhoons to Defend Saudi Cities from Houthi Attacks
articles.summary: British PM Andy Burnham and the Ministry of Defence announced RAF Typhoon jets will deploy to protect Saudi Arabian cities and infrastructure from Houthi aerial attacks. The jets will operate defensively, intercepting drones and missiles without offensive strikes, to ensure regional stability and secure vital energy trade routes amid rising tensions, expanding British support for Riyadh.

articles.headline: Kuki Man Killed in Manipur, Shutdowns Intensify After Meitei Deaths
articles.summary: A 45-year-old Kuki tribesman was shot dead in Manipur's Kangpokpi, a day after three Meitei villagers were ambushed and killed, leading to three Kuki-Zo arrests. This intensified outrage in Imphal Valley and prompted calls for total shutdowns and strikes, paralyzing the city. The Committee on Tribal Unity blamed NSCN-IM and Zeliangrong United Front for the Kuki man's death.

articles.headline: Delhi Sweet Units Show Hygiene Lapses Ahead of Diwali Inspections
articles.summary: Ahead of Diwali, Delhi government’s Food Safety Department inspections found significant hygiene, cleanliness, and storage lapses at several sweet manufacturing units across the Capital. Issues included pest activity, food handlers without gloves, open dustbins, and improper food storage. Samples of sweets, milk, and milk-based items were collected for testing and analysis.

articles.headline: US Secretary Rubio: India-US "Perfectly Aligned" on Core Strategic Issues
articles.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio affirmed India and the U.S. are "perfectly aligned" on core national interests, viewing their relationship as an "extraordinary strategic partnership" in technology, trade, security, and energy, despite disagreements. He emphasized their joint commitment to dismantling terrorist networks, securing justice for victims, and ensuring a secure Indo-Pacific and diversified energy portfolios.

articles.headline: Harmanpreet Kaur's 91* Powers India to 3-0 T20I Series Sweep
articles.summary: Skipper Harmanpreet Kaur's blistering unbeaten 91 off 41 balls (10x4s, 6x6s) and Shafali Verma's entertaining 69 off 37 balls powered India to 216/7. This led to a commanding 92-run victory over Zimbabwe in the final T20I, securing a 3-0 series sweep for India.

articles.headline: Bavuma's Career-Best 179 Puts South Africa in Command Against Australia
articles.summary: Temba Bavuma's career-best 179 and Kagiso Rabada's 85 led a dramatic South African fightback against Australia on Day 3 of the second Test at St George's Park. South Africa declared their first innings at 425/9 in 127.1 overs. Rabada then took an early wicket, leaving Australia at 3/1 by stumps.

articles.headline: Arafat Minhas' All-Round Show Powers Pakistan to Tri-Series Win
articles.summary: All-rounder Arafat Minhas delivered a stellar performance in the ODI tri-series in Rawalpindi, scoring a maiden half-century (59) and taking a career-best six wickets (6-40). His all-round show anchored Pakistan to 302/9, leading to a convincing 87-run win as England was bowled out for 215 in 38.4 overs.

articles.headline: Maddison Returns, Scores as Tottenham Ends Premier League Winless Run
articles.summary: James Maddison made a sensational return to Tottenham's starting lineup after 17 months out due to injury, scoring an early goal as Roberto De Zerbi’s men beat Coventry 3-1. This victory marked Tottenham's first Premier League win of the season. Separately, Lazio also secured a significant 3-0 win against Juventus in Turin.
